summary: Ruling was latest judicial rebuke of unprecedented efforts from Trump administration to intervene in elections process of multiple states Supreme court rules against Trump over bid to force California to set aside ballots Sign up for the Breaking News US email
summary_zh: 最高法院的裁决是对特朗普政府干预多个州选举进程的前所未有的司法谴责
body_en: The US supreme court on Monday quickly rejected the Trump administration’s request to force California to set aside thousands of mail ballots from people President Donald Trump’s administration claims are noncitizens , the Associated Press reports.

The high court refused to intervene in a case involving 20,000 people the Republican administration flagged as likely noncitizens on the largely Democratic state’s voter rolls. The decision came just hours after the administration asked the supreme court to intervene.

The ruling was the latest judicial rebuke in the face of a wave of unprecedented efforts from the Trump administration to intervene in the elections process of multiple states. The midterm elections are expected to bring nationwide victories for Democrats and impose more Congressional checks on Trump’s power.

In California, the Trump administration had asked the high court to set aside the challenged ballots until the voters’ citizenship status could be verified. But officials there said that the list appeared to be filled with errors and that setting the ballots aside could effectively disenfranchise legal voters.

The high court did not detail its reasoning for rejecting the Trump administration’s request, as is common in emergency decisions. The justices previously rejected Trump’s push to restrict mail ballots around the country in September, even though the justices have sided with his administration in a series of other emergency docket appeals.
body_zh: 据美联社报道，美国最高法院周一迅速驳回了特朗普政府的要求，要求加州搁置数千张邮寄选票，这些选票来自唐纳德·特朗普总统政府声称的非公民。
高等法院拒绝干预涉及 20,000 人的案件，共和党政府在这个以民主党为主的州的选民名册上将其标记为可能非公民。这一决定是在政府要求最高法院干预后几个小时做出的。
面对特朗普政府前所未有的干预多个州选举进程的浪潮，这一裁决是最新的司法谴责。中期选举预计将为民主党带来全国性的胜利，并对特朗普的权力施加更多国会制衡。
在加利福尼亚州，特朗普政府已要求高等法院搁置受到质疑的选票，直到选民的公民身份得到核实。但那里的官员表示，这份名单似乎充满了错误，将选票搁置可能实际上剥夺了合法选民的选举权。
高等法院没有详细说明拒绝特朗普政府请求的理由，这在紧急决定中很常见。法官们此前拒绝了特朗普9月份在全国范围内限制邮寄选票的推动，尽管法官们在一系列其他紧急上诉中支持了特朗普政府。

title_en: Trump promised a steel mill in this rural Iowa region. But is it all a midterm election ploy?
title_zh: 特朗普承诺在爱荷华州的这个农村地区建造一家钢铁厂。但这都是中期选举的策略吗？

body_en: Trump promised a steel mill in this rural Iowa region. But is it all a midterm election ploy?
Residents would welcome the development, but the president’s past false promises cast doubt on the proposal

O n a Monday afternoon in late September, Donald Trump gathered Iowa Republicans in the Oval Office to make a big announcement: the firm Mesabi Metallics would invest $15bn to make the midwestern state the site of the largest steel mill in the country.

One month later, and just days before the midterm election, word has spread in the small town of Wever, population 142, that the mill will be built somewhere nearby. And that’s been about it – no shovels in the dirt, workers on a job site or machinery on the dirt roads leading down towards the Mississippi River.
Ask about the project in town, and the reaction isn’t enthusiasm, but skepticism.
This Georgia county is one of the US’s most diverse – and that could flip multiple elections
“More jobs,” Missy Pollpeter, 52, said of the project’s potential as she dined at the Green Bay Bar and Grill, Wever’s only restaurant.
“If they bring it here,” her husband, Mike Pollpeter, 60, said as he finished a burger.

On paper, a steel mill seems like a great development for a corner of Iowa that has a long history both of manufacturing and the disinvestment that has struck so much of the industrial midwest. According to the White House, the project would create 6,000 jobs during its construction and then 1,750 when it is complete, and generate $95bn in economic activity.

What people can’t get over is how the project was debuted, and who was announced it. The president made the plan public just over a month before Tuesday’s midterm elections, when Iowa will play a major role in determining if Democrats regain control of Congress amid Trump’s downbeat approval ratings . Wever itself lies in a congressional district that is viewed as the most competitive in the state.
And then there’s the fact that Trump has a history of making proclamations that don’t quite pan out.

“Remember Foxconn?” asked Jeff Thompson as he served drinks at Green Bay “Bottoms Up”, the town’s only bar. Foxconn is the electronics manufacturing giant that Trump famously declared would build a massive factory in neighboring Wisconsin during his first term, only for the project to wind up flopping .

A similar situation may be playing out elsewhere this year. Just days after debuting plans for the Iowa steel mill, the president said South Korea would invest $54bn in building a long-discussed natural gas pipeline in Alaska, only for officials in Seoul to say they’d agreed to no such deal .
But Iowa’s Republican-controlled legislature was undeterred, and quickly approved $1.4bn in tax breaks to make the mill happen.

Charles Sutton, a spokesperson for Mesabi, a Minnesota-based firm that is part of the Indian conglomerate Essar Group, said they are on track to produce steel by 2030 from a site in “eastern Iowa”, the location of which will be announced “in the very near future”.
“The project is in active development with strong momentum,” Sutton said. “We anticipate being able to make several announcements in the coming weeks in line with the project schedule.”

Mariannette Miller-Meeks, the Republican who represents south-eastern Iowa, said that “the project is for sure happening”. Elected to a third term in 2024 by less than 800 votes, she is a top target of Democrats this year as they vie to regain control of Congress’s lower chamber.

As she campaigned in Fort Madison, 10 minutes south of Wever, Miller-Meeks credited Trump’s tariff regime and his major domestic policy bill with making the project possible, but said that the details of the mill are under negotiation between the county and Mesabi. “It will be on the outcome of those negotiations, but it will be coming to south-east Iowa,” she said.
Skepticism mires Trump’s Iowa steel plant project: ‘Promises are not the same as jobs’

Blaine Watkins, a Republican who represents the area in the state legislature, said the mill would “completely change” Lee county, where Trump won almost two-thirds of the vote in 2024. Talks to make it happen had been going on for seven or eight months, he said, and he had a hard time believing they wouldn’t come to fruition.
body_zh: 特朗普承诺在爱荷华州的这个农村地区建造一家钢铁厂。但这都是中期选举的策略吗？
居民们会欢迎这一开发项目，但总统过去的虚假承诺使人们对该提议产生了怀疑
9 月下旬的一个星期一下午，唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 在椭圆形办公室召集爱荷华州共和党人，宣布一项重大公告：梅萨比金属公司 (Mesabi Metallics) 将投资 150 亿美元，让这个中西部州成为美国最大的钢厂。
一个月后，就在中期选举前几天，有消息在人口 142 人的韦弗小镇上传开，工厂将建在附近的某个地方。事情就是这样——泥土中没有铲子，工地上没有工人，通往密西西比河的土路上没有机械。
当询问镇上的这个项目时，人们的反应不是热情，而是怀疑。
佐治亚州的这个县是美国最多元化的县之一，这可能会颠覆多次选举
“更多的就业机会，”52 岁的米西·波尔彼得 (Missy Pollpeter) 在韦弗唯一的餐厅 Green Bay Bar and Grill 用餐时谈到了该项目的潜力。
“如果他们把它带到这里来，”她 60 岁的丈夫迈克·波尔彼得 (Mike Pollpeter) 吃完汉堡后说道。
从表面上看，对于爱荷华州的一个角落来说，一座钢厂似乎是一项伟大的发展，该州的制造业和投资撤资历史悠久，中西部工业区的大部分地区都受到了影响。据白宫称，该项目将在建设期间创造 6,000 个就业岗位，竣工后将创造 1,750 个就业岗位，并产生 950 亿美元的经济活动。
人们无法理解的是这个项目是如何推出的，以及由谁宣布的。总统在周二中期选举前一个月公布了该计划，届时爱荷华州将在决定民主党是否在特朗普悲观支持率的情况下重新获得国会控制权方面发挥重要作用。韦弗本身位于被视为该州最具竞争力的国会选区。
事实上，特朗普有发表不太成功的声明的历史。
“还记得富士康吗？”杰夫·汤普森 (Jeff Thompson) 在绿湾“Bottoms Up”（该镇唯一的酒吧）提供饮料时问道。富士康是电子制造巨头，特朗普曾宣称将在其第一个任期内在邻近的威斯康星州建造一座大型工厂，但该项目最终以失败告终。
今年其他地方可能也会出现类似的情况。就在爱荷华州钢厂计划公布几天后，总统表示韩国将投资 540 亿美元在阿拉斯加建设一条讨论已久的天然气管道，但首尔官员表示他们不同意达成此类协议。
但爱荷华州共和党控制的立法机构并没有被吓倒，并迅速批准了 14 亿美元的税收减免，以使工厂得以建成。
总部位于明尼苏达州的 Mesabi 公司隶属于印度企业集团 Essar Group，其发言人查尔斯·萨顿 (Charles Sutton) 表示，他们有望在 2030 年之前在“爱荷华州东部”的一个地点生产钢铁，该地点将在“不久的将来”公布。
“该项目正在积极开发，势头强劲，”萨顿说。 “我们预计能够在未来几周内根据项目时间表发布几项公告。”
代表爱荷华州东南部的共和党人玛丽安内特·米勒-米克斯表示，“该项目肯定会发生”。她以不到 800 票的优势在 2024 年第三次当选，是民主党今年争夺国会下议院控制权的首要目标。
米勒-米克斯在距韦弗以南 10 分钟车程的麦迪逊堡进行竞选活动时，她称赞特朗普的关税制度及其主要国内政策法案使该项目成为可能，但表示该工厂的细节正在该县与梅萨比之间进行谈判。 “这将取决于这些谈判的结果，但它将发生在爱荷华州东南部，”她说。
特朗普的爱荷华钢铁厂项目陷入怀疑：“承诺与就业并不相同”
代表该地区的州立法机关的共和党人布莱恩·沃特金斯 (Blaine Watkins) 表示，该工厂将“彻底改变”李县，特朗普在 2024 年在那里赢得了近三分之二的选票。他说，为实现这一目标的谈判已经进行了七八个月，他很难相信谈判不会取得成果。

body_en: Trump unveils results of $14m reflecting pool makeover in final appeal before midterms | Donald Trump
Trump unveils results of $14m reflecting pool makeover in final appeal before midterms
US president shares delayed results of chaotic renovation on DC site as Americans prepare to head to the polls

Donald Trump unveiled the delayed results of his $14m renovation of Washington DC’s Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool in what is expected to be his final press conference before voters head to the polls for the midterm elections.

On the eve of a consequential election day, with polls indicating that most voters feel the US president has grown too focused on building projects in the nation’s capital, he stood in front of the newly opened reflecting pool to discuss – in detail – changes to the pool’s pipe, the grass surrounding the area and granite.
“This project should be a project that unites all Americans,” Trump told reporters on Monday afternoon.

It has proven anything but. After Trump’s first revealed his “beautiful” makeover of the reflecting pool in June, a massive algae bloom turned it green (instead of the promised “American flag blue”) and the coating started to peel away.

Trump alleged that vandals were to blame, although his administration failed to produce evidence to substantiate such claims. While former Olympic canoeist David Hearn was initially charged over alleged damage, the office of the US attorney Jeanine Pirro later dropped the case, infuriating the president.
Hearn’s attorneys said the case’s dismissal “does not erase the abuse of government power in arresting and charging a patriotic American who did nothing wrong”.

On Monday, Trump accused his Democratic predecessors, Joe Biden and Barack Obama, of overspending on previous renovations to the reflecting pool and once again, without evidence, accused vandals of purposefully damaging the Trump administration’s renovations.

Roughly 20 minutes into his remarks on the reflecting pool, less than 24 hours before Americans head to the polls, Trump pivoted to acknowledge Tuesday’s midterm elections, which he declared to be crucial.
The party of a sitting president often loses seats during the midterms, he noted. “We gave this a very strong shot,” Trump said.
For weeks, polls have shown Democratic candidates are narrowly ahead of Republican candidates in key races – that includes competitive Senate races in Texas, Alaska, Kansas, Iowa and Maine.
Voters have expressed dissatisfaction with Trump’s handling of his job as president, particularly over the US economy and cost of living.

The prices of gas and groceries have risen since the beginning of the year, and inflation has remained stubbornly high – largely the result of the war with Iran that Trump started at the end of February.
body_zh: 特朗普在中期选举前的最终上诉中公布了 1400 万美元的结果，反映出资金池的改造唐纳德·特朗普
特朗普在中期选举前的最终上诉中公布了 1400 万美元的结果，反映了资金池的改造
当美国人准备前往投票站时，美国总统分享了华盛顿工地混乱翻修的延迟结果
唐纳德·特朗普在选民前往中期选举投票站之前的最后一次新闻发布会上公布了耗资 1400 万美元的华盛顿特区林肯纪念堂倒影池翻修工程的延迟结果，预计这将是他的最后一次新闻发布会。
在选举日的前夕，民意调查显示，大多数选民认为美国总统过于专注于首都的建设项目，他站在新开放的倒影池前，详细讨论了对水池管道、周围草地和花岗岩的改造。
“这个项目应该是一个团结所有美国人的项目，”特朗普周一下午对记者说。
但事实证明并非如此。六月，特朗普首次透露了他对倒影池的“美丽”改造后，大量藻类的繁殖将其变成了绿色（而不是承诺的“美国国旗蓝色”），并且涂层开始剥落。
特朗普声称破坏行为是罪魁祸首，尽管他的政府未能提供证据证实这种说法。虽然前奥运会皮划艇运动员大卫·赫恩最初因涉嫌造成损害而受到指控，但美国检察官珍妮·皮罗的办公室后来撤销了此案，这激怒了总统。
赫恩的律师表示，该案被驳回“并不能消除政府滥用权力逮捕和指控一名没有做错任何事的爱国美国人的行为”。
周一，特朗​​普指责他的民主党前任乔·拜登和巴拉克·奥巴马在之前的倒影池翻修工程中超支，并在没有证据的情况下再次指责破坏者故意破坏特朗普政府的翻修工程。
特朗普在反思池发表讲话大约 20 分钟后，距离美国人前往投票站不到 24 小时，他转而承认周二的中期选举，他宣称这次选举至关重要。
他指出，现任总统所在的政党经常在中期选举期间失去席位。特朗普说：“我们对此进行了非常有力的尝试。”
几周来，民意调查显示，民主党候选人在关键竞选中以微弱优势领先于共和党候选人，其中包括德克萨斯州、阿拉斯加州、堪萨斯州、爱荷华州和缅因州竞争激烈的参议院竞选。
选民对特朗普处理总统工作的方式表示不满，特别是对美国经济和生活成本的不满。
自今年年初以来，天然气和食品杂货的价格不断上涨，通货膨胀率居高不下 — — 这主要是特朗普在二月底发动的与伊朗的战争的结果。

title_en: Judge accuses DOJ of 'weaponization,' tosses case against ex-FBI officials
title_zh: 法官指控司法部“武器化”，驳回针对前联邦调查局官员的案件
summary: The judge said he was "deeply troubled" by the mistakes and rushed nature of the case over the FBI's Hunter Biden probes — one of several politically charged DOJ actions ahead of the midterms.
summary_zh: 法官表示，他对联邦调查局亨特·拜登调查中的错误和仓促性质感到“深感不安”——这是几起政治性调查之一
body_en: Judge accuses DOJ of 'weaponization,' tosses case against ex-FBI officials
Magistrate Judge Zia M. Faruqui speaks before a debate at the Prettyman Federal Courthouse in Washington, D.C. in November 2024. Craig Hudson/The Washington Post via Getty Images hide caption

A federal magistrate judge on Monday dismissed the Justice Department's criminal case against two former FBI officials charged in connection with the bureau's investigations into former President Joe Biden's son.

Bradley Benavides and Nikki Floris were charged around two weeks ago with lying to Congress in 2023 about their knowledge of the FBI's investigations into Biden's son, Hunter Biden. It is one of several politically charged actions by the Justice Department under President Trump in the run-up to the midterm elections on Tuesday.

At a hearing in federal court in Washington, D.C., U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui castigated the government's investigation into Floris and Benavides, describing it as rushed and riddled with errors.
Politics, norms and the DOJ's unprecedented pre-election headlines
"I am deeply troubled by what has happened here," Faruqui said in a scathing ruling from the bench. "What transpired here cannot be described as anything other than weaponization."

The court's ruling came after a days-long preliminary hearing last week to determine whether probable cause existed to charge Floris and Benavides with lying to Congress. It featured testimony from one of the FBI agents who investigated the case.

In a statement, a Justice Department spokesperson said the department "disagrees with the Magistrate's decision, which remarkably appears to suggest that high-ranking government officials are immune from accountability for making materially false statements to Congress."

"We are evaluating all options but cannot comment further on an ongoing criminal investigation," the spokesperson said. "The Department's actions will continue to be guided by the facts, the evidence, and the law—not politics."
Over the course of an hour, Faruqui on Monday laid out the basis for his decision before a packed courtroom that included many former senior FBI officials.

The judge noted that the investigation into Floris and Benavides was opened on FBI Director Kash Patel's orders the day after President Trump delivered a primetime address on national TV in mid-July. In that speech, Trump repeated his false claims about fraud in the 2020 election and urged the FBI to investigate.
In primetime speech, Trump doesn't provide evidence for illegal voting

Faruqui noted that the alleged false statements were made to Congress in 2023, yet the Justice Department waited three years to pursue the case. Prosecutors then brought charges some two weeks before the midterm elections, despite a DOJ policy prohibiting timing any action to influence an election.

That was not the only unusual decision by the department. The judge also noted that charges were filed as a criminal complaint, a document usually used when there is some need for urgency such as an imminent danger, a statute of limitations deadline or a risk of flight—none of which existed in this case.
The only event that was looming here, he said, was the midterms.
"I will not bury my head in the sand and pretend I cannot read a calendar," Faruqui said. "I will not lobotomize myself that way."
Ex-FBI employees charged with lying to Congress over Hunter Biden inquiries
He also said prosecutors appear not to want to take this case before a grand jury, perhaps given the Justice Department's poor track record recently with grand juries in Washington, D.C.
On several occasions under the Trump administration, grand juries in the nation's capital have refused to return indictments in high-profile, politically charged cases.
body_zh: 法官指控司法部“武器化”，驳回针对前联邦调查局官员的案件
2024 年 11 月，治安法官齐亚·M·法鲁基 (Zia M. Faruqui) 在华盛顿特区普雷特曼联邦法院举行的辩论前发表讲话。克雷格·哈德森 (Craig Hudson)/《华盛顿邮报》，盖蒂图片社 隐藏标题栏
周一，一名联邦治安法官驳回了司法部对两名前联邦调查局官员的刑事诉讼，这两名前联邦调查局官员被指控与该局对前总统乔·拜登儿子的调查有关。
大约两周前，布拉德利·贝纳维德斯 (Bradley Benavides) 和尼基·弗洛里斯 (Nikki Floris) 被指控在 2023 年向国会撒谎，谎称他们了解联邦调查局对拜登之子亨特·拜登的调查。这是特朗普总统领导下的司法部在周二中期选举前采取的几项带有政治色彩的行动之一。
在华盛顿特区联邦法院的听证会上，美国治安法官齐亚·法鲁基严厉批评了政府对弗洛里斯和贝纳维德斯的调查，称其仓促且充满错误。
政治、规范和司法部前所未有的选前头条新闻
法鲁基在法官的严厉裁决中表示：“我对这里发生的事情深感不安。” “这里发生的事情只能被描述为武器化。”
法院在上周进行了为期几​​天的初步听证会后做出了裁决，以确定是否存在指控弗洛里斯和贝纳维德斯向国会撒谎的合理理由。它收录了一名调查此案的联邦调查局特工的证词。
司法部发言人在一份声明中表示，该部门“不同意治安法官的决定，这显然表明政府高级官员可以免受向国会做出重大虚假陈述的责任”。
该发言人表示：“我们正在评估所有选项，但无法对正在进行的刑事调查进一步发表评论。” “司法部的行动将继续以事实、证据和法律为指导，而不是政治。”
在一个小时的时间里，法鲁基周一在挤满了人的法庭上阐述了他的决定的依据，其中包括许多前联邦调查局高级官员。
法官指出，在特朗普总统于 7 月中旬在国家电视台发表黄金时段讲话的第二天，联邦调查局局长卡什·帕特尔下令对弗洛里斯和贝纳维德斯展开调查。在那次演讲中，特朗普重申了他关于 2020 年大选舞弊的虚假说法，并敦促 FBI 进行调查。
特朗普在黄金时段演讲中没有提供非法投票的证据
法鲁基指出，涉嫌虚假陈述是在 2023 年向国会做出的，但司法部等了三年才追查此案。尽管司法部的政策禁止采取任何影响选举的行动，但检察官随后在中期选举前大约两周提出指控。
这并不是该部门唯一的不寻常决定。法官还指出，指控是作为刑事申诉提出的，这种文件通常在紧急情况下使用，例如迫在眉睫的危险、时效期限或潜逃风险，而本案中不存在这些情况。
他说，这里即将发生的唯一事件是中期选举。
“我不会把头埋在沙子里，假装我看不懂日历，”法鲁基说。 “我不会那样对自己进行脑白质切除术。”
前联邦调查局雇员被控在亨特·拜登调查中向国会撒谎
他还表示，检察官似乎不想在大陪审团面前审理此案，这可能是考虑到司法部最近在华盛顿特区大陪审团中的不良记录。
在特朗普政府执政期间，美国首都的大陪审团曾多次拒绝对备受瞩目的政治指控案件发出起诉书。

body_en: Judge tosses case against two officials accused of lying about Hunter Biden | FBI
Judge tosses case against two officials accused of lying about Hunter Biden
The two FBI agents were charged with making false statements to Congress while testifying about the bureau’s role in investigating Biden’s laptop

A federal judge dismissed criminal charges against two former FBI officials who were accused of lying about their involvement in the investigation into Hunter Biden , the son of former president Joe Biden, on Monday.
Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui said prosecutors failed to show probable cause that the two former officials, Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, had knowingly made false statements.
Faruqui also suggested prosecutors purposefully brought the charges at a sensitive time, just 10 days before the midterm elections.

“What has transpired here cannot be described as anything other than weaponization,” Faruqui said during the court hearing. “I will ​not bury ​my head in the sand and pretend I cannot read a calendar.”

The judge criticized federal prosecutors for rushing the prosecution and making “critical mistakes”. Faruqui said that some of the former officials’ ​statements were not actually false and others could be attributed to “honest mistakes of memory”.
Federal prosecutors in Washington DC charged Floris and Benavides last month with making false statements to members of Congress in 2023 while testifying to the House judiciary committee.
The two former officials were testifying about the bureau’s role in investigating the contents of a laptop that belonged to Hunter Biden.

Floris and Benavides served on an FBI taskforce that examined potential foreign influence in American politics. The taskforce was initially formed after the 2016 presidential election when officials raised concerns that Russia attempted to interfere with the election.

The FBI taskforce had raised concerns in the lead-up to the 2020 presidential election that Russia could have engaged in another disinformation operation to assist Donald Trump’s campaign by bolstering claims about Hunter Biden’s laptop.

Last week, an FBI agent testified last week ​that the probe into Floris and ‌Benavides began with the president’s ​primetime address in July on election ​security, during which he announced the FBI would investigate whether US intelligence agencies had suppressed information about Chinese meddling in the 2020 election.

The next day, the FBI director, Kash Patel , tasked the bureau’s Kansas City field office with scrutinizing Floris, who had cast doubt on an FBI intelligence report claiming that China sought to interfere in the 2020 election to boost Joe Biden over Trump.
Trump has publicly criticized individuals that he believes undermined his efforts to overturn the 2020 presidential results.

But since returning to office in January 2025, the justice department has targeted people that Trump views as enemies through indictments and complaints. However, some high-profile attempts have failed to bear fruit.
While the justice department’s complaint against Floris and Benavides has been dismissed, prosecutors could try to charge them again by asking a grand jury to review evidence and approve charges.

治安法官齐亚·法鲁基表示，检察官未能证明两名前官员尼基·弗洛里斯和布拉德利·贝纳维德斯故意做出虚假陈述的合理理由。

法官批评联邦检察官仓促起诉并犯下“严重错误”。法鲁基表示，一些前官员的言论实际上并非虚假，另一些则可能归因于“无意识的记忆错误”。
华盛顿特区的联邦检察官上个月指控弗洛里斯和贝纳维德斯在 2023 年向众议院司法委员会作证时向国会议员做出虚假陈述。
这两名前官员正在就该局在调查亨特·拜登一台笔记本电脑内容中所扮演的角色作证。
弗洛里斯和贝纳维德斯曾在联邦调查局特别工作组任职，负责调查外国对美国政治的潜在影响。该工作组最初是在 2016 年总统选举后成立的，当时官员们担心俄罗斯试图干预选举。
联邦调查局特别工作组在 2020 年总统选举前夕曾提出担忧，认为俄罗斯可能参与另一场虚假信息行动，通过支持有关亨特·拜登笔记本电脑的说法来协助唐纳德·特朗普的竞选活动。
上周，一名联邦调查局特工作证说，对弗洛里斯和贝纳维德斯的调查始于总统 7 月份关于选举安全的黄金时段讲话，期间他宣布联邦调查局将调查美国情报机构是否压制了有关中国干预 2020 年选举的信息。
第二天，FBI 局长卡什·帕特尔 (Kash Patel) 责成该局堪萨斯城外地办事处对弗洛里斯进行审查，弗洛里斯对联邦调查局情报报告提出质疑，该报告称中国试图干预 2020 年大选，以推动乔·拜登击败特朗普。
特朗普曾公开批评一些他认为破坏了他推翻 2020 年总统选举结果的努力的个人。
但自2025年1月重新上任以来，司法部通过起诉和投诉将特朗普视为敌人的人作为目标。然而，一些高调的尝试却未能取得成果。
虽然司法部对弗洛里斯和贝纳维德斯的投诉已被驳回，但检察官可以通过要求大陪审团审查证据并批准指控来尝试再次指控他们。

body_en: ‘A despicable betrayal’: Democrats incensed by Haley Stevens’s endorsement of Mike Rogers
Stevens’s decision sparked fierce backlash from members of the party, while Donald Trump praised the sudden switch

Democrat Haley Stevens’s shocking last-minute endorsement of Mike Rogers, the Michigan Republican Senate candidate, in the run-up to Tuesday’s midterm elections has sparked fierce backlash from members of her party.

Stevens, who narrowly lost in the Democratic primary for Senate to Abdul El-Sayed, announced her support for Rogers after a feud with the El-Sayed campaign over an outside group’s advertisement, which blamed the high cost of living on US support for Israel.
Democrat Haley Stevens endorses Abdul El-Sayed’s Republican rival Mike Rogers

Following the extraordinary public rupture on Sunday, El-Sayed’s campaign said it raised more than $2.4m, a fundraising record in the final days of a race that could determine control of the US senate. The Democrat’s campaign said more than 26,000 people contributed for the first time on Sunday.
New York Democrat Chuck Schumer, the Senate minority leader, described Stevens’ endorsement of Rogers as “a despicable betrayal”.

“Senate Democrats are united in our support for Abdul El-Sayed, because we know he will fight for the economic interests of working families in Michigan, unlike Mike Rogers, who is a tool of Donald Trump and billionaire donors,” Schumer posted on social media.
Nancy Pelosi, the Democratic former House speaker, posted that Stevens had “chosen to dangerously betray Michigan families’ healthcare, freedoms and future with her horrific endorsement”.
The New York mayor, Zohran Mamdani, said that “working class people’s lives are on the ballot on Tuesday”.
“Haley Stevens just betrayed them by endorsing the very Republican she said she wanted to run against,” Mamdani posted .

Stevens refused to clearly explain what led to her endorsement of Rogers in an interview with Anderson Cooper on CNN Sunday evening . “I’m just casting my one vote this way,” Stevens said, while insisting she still wanted Democrats to win the majority on election day.

“I am not trying to upset anyone,” she added. “I’m just being honest with my constituents and what I’m hearing from people, and in fact, I’ve been hearing from a ton of Dems, Anderson, who said: ‘Thank you, this is how we felt; we haven’t liked this campaign; it’s painful.’”

Cooper pressed Stevens, questioning whether being disinvited from El-Sayed’s campaign event triggered her endorsement of Rogers. At one point, Stevens refused to answer the question, allowing several seconds of silence to air.

Stevens has continued to defend her decision as she faces accusations of betrayal from Democrats, including calls for her expulsion from the House caucus. Several members of her congressional staff resigned in protest. In an interview on Monday, she compared herself with Pennsylvania Senator John Fetterman, a one-time progressive who now frequently breaks with his party, especially over supporting Israel.
“You see a Democrat from Pennsylvania, you know, his name’s a lightning rod in the party. His name’s Fetterman,” she told conservative commentator Scott Jennings. “They say the same thing about him.”
Curtis Hertel, the chair the Michigan Democratic party, said in a post that Stevens was not a member of the party “nor will she be in the future”.
A Detroit journalist, Sam Robinson, shared a video in which Hertel was asked why he thought Stevens made the endorsement.

“Obviously there are sour grapes from the election, but there is no reasonable explanation for this. I have known Haley Stevens for a long time, and I know what she has fought for her in her career, and this is the antithesis of all of that,” Hertel said.
Debbie Dingell, a veteran Michigan House Democrat, dismissed Stevens’s endorsement as a distraction from voters’ concerns about the cost of living.
body_zh: “卑鄙的背叛”：海莉·史蒂文斯对迈克·罗杰斯的支持激怒了民主党人
史蒂文斯的决定引发了党内成员的强烈反对，而唐纳德·特朗普则赞扬了这一突然转变
民主党人海莉·史蒂文斯在周二中期选举前的最后一刻令人震惊地支持密歇根州共和党参议院候选人迈克·罗杰斯，这引发了党内成员的强烈反对。
史蒂文斯在民主党参议院初选中以微弱优势输给阿卜杜勒·赛义德。在与赛义德竞选团队因外部团体的广告发生争执后，史蒂文斯宣布支持罗杰斯，该广告将高生活成本归咎于美国对以色列的支持。
民主党人海莉·史蒂文斯支持阿卜杜勒·赛义德的共和党对手迈克·罗杰斯
在周日非同寻常的公开决裂之后，埃尔-赛义德的竞选团队表示，已筹集了超过 240 万美元，这是这场可能决定美国参议院控制权的竞选最后几天的筹款记录。民主党竞选团队表示，周日有超过 26,000 人首次捐款。
参议院少数党领袖、纽约民主党人查克·舒默将史蒂文斯对罗杰斯的支持描述为“卑鄙的背叛”。
舒默在社交媒体上发帖称：“参议院民主党人团结一致支持阿卜杜勒·赛义德，因为我们知道他将为密歇根州工薪家庭的经济利益而战，这与唐纳德·特朗普和亿万富翁捐助者的工具迈克·罗杰斯不同。”
民主党前众议院议长南希·佩洛西 (Nancy Pelosi) 发帖称，史蒂文斯“选择以她可怕的支持来危险地背叛密歇根州家庭的医疗保健、自由和未来”。
纽约市长佐兰·马姆达尼 (Zohran Mamdani) 表示，“周二的选票将决定工人阶级人民的生活”。
“海莉·史蒂文斯只是背叛了他们，她支持了她说她想竞选的共和党人，”马姆达尼发帖说。
周日晚上，史蒂文斯在接受美国有线电视新闻网安德森·库珀采访时拒绝明确解释是什么原因导致她支持罗杰斯。 “我只是这样投一票，”史蒂文斯说，同时坚称她仍然希望民主党在选举日赢得多数席位。
“我并不是想让任何人感到不安，”她补充道。 “我只是对我的选民和我从人们那里听到的事情诚实，事实上，我已经听到很多民主党人安德森说：‘谢谢，这就是我们的感受；我们不喜欢这场竞选；这很痛苦。’”
库珀向史蒂文斯施压，质疑取消参加埃尔赛义德竞选活动的邀请是否会引发她对罗杰斯的支持。有一次，史蒂文斯拒绝回答这个问题，让空气中出现了几秒钟的沉默。
史蒂文斯继续为自己的决定辩护，因为她面临民主党的背叛指控，包括要求将她驱逐出众议院核心小组的呼声。她的几名国会工作人员辞职以示抗议。在周一的一次采访中，她将自己与宾夕法尼亚州参议员约翰·费特曼进行了比较，费特曼曾经是一位进步人士，现在经常与他的政党决裂，尤其是在支持以色列方面。
“你看到一位来自宾夕法尼亚州的民主党人，你知道，他的名字是党内的避雷针。他的名字叫费特曼，”她告诉保守派评论员斯科特·詹宁斯。 “他们对他也这么说。”
密歇根州民主党主席柯蒂斯·赫特尔(Curtis Hertel)在一篇帖子中表示，史蒂文斯不是该党党员，“未来也不会”。
底特律记者萨姆·罗宾逊分享了一段视频，视频中赫特尔被问到为什么他认为史蒂文斯做了背书。
“显然选举有酸葡萄心理，但对此没有合理的解释。我认识海莉·史蒂文斯很长时间了，我知道她在职业生涯中为了什么而奋斗，而这正是所有这一切的对立面，”赫特尔说。
密歇根州众议院民主党资深人士黛比·丁格尔(Debbie Dingell)认为史蒂文斯的支持分散了选民对生活成本的担忧。

title_en: ‘A lot of Republicans have held their tongues’: Anger at Trump is growing
title_zh: “很多共和党人都保持沉默”：对特朗普的愤怒正在增长
summary: Few Republicans are willing to publicly lambast the president. But they’re more blunt in private.
summary_zh: 很少有共和党人愿意公开痛斥总统。但他们私下里却更加直率。
body_en: Republicans are already privately blaming President Donald Trump as they brace for losses on Tuesday.

Even as they race to distance themselves from his actions on tariffs, the unpopular Iran war and his mass deportation agenda, few have been willing to criticize him publicly — a clear sign of just how powerful Trump's grip remains on the GOP. But interviews with roughly a dozen candidates, campaign officials and lawmakers reveal they're acutely aware of who, exactly, put them on the back foot this entire cycle.

"There was a point earlier this year where we really felt like we could defy history," said one House Republican, who, like others in this article, was granted anonymity to candidly discuss midterms dynamics. "And then Trump bombed Iran. And it was just one thing after another.”

Republicans are tied or trailing in polls in numerous critical battlegrounds and expecting to lose some once-secure red seats. And Trump's unfocused closing message — including repeated comments about male candidates' physical appearances — has further frustrated an already on-edge party.

“I think Jon Husted's ass and Nicki Minaj's is a great closing message,” T.W. Arrighi, a Republican strategist working on the South Carolina Senate race and others, said sarcastically in an interview on The Conversation with Dasha Burns . “You’ve got to take the good with the bad with Trump, unless you want to drive yourself crazy every day.”
“People are gonna go after the president. The buck stops with him. His approval ratings aren't great,” he added.
Privately, some Republicans are even harsher. “At least when Barack Obama was president, he only screwed his enemies, never his friends,” said a second House Republican.

The White House defended its involvement in the war with Iran, tariff regime and approach to immigration enforcement. Davis Ingle, a White House spokesperson, said in a statement that Trump “is the unequivocal leader, best messenger, and unmatched motivator for the Republican Party, and he is committed to maintaining Republican majorities in Congress.”
One White House official, granted anonymity to speak candidly, called the blame game “an asinine adventure” and said Trump “has obviously left it all on the field.”

If the bottom falls out for the GOP on Tuesday, the quiet calls assigning him blame may turn into a public shanking as Trump nears the lame-duck stage of his presidency, Republicans refocus on how to win voters back for 2028 and jostle for their own spots in the party’s future.

“I'm not sure what the Republican Party looks like in six months. Look, a lot of Republicans have held their tongues. A lot of Republicans who have real problems with the way things have gone the last two years have been good soldiers,” said a Republican strategist involved in competitive midterm races across the country. “But what happens if we lose 35 House seats and six Senate seats?”
“We all know who the problem is. It’s Trump. And do we continue down a path of losing?” the strategist added.

In Georgia, some Republicans have already warned that low early voting turnout in rural parts of the state could drag down their entire ticket. "If you live in rural Georgia, you're going to be disproportionately hurt by higher — especially diesel — prices,” said Jason Shepherd, the former GOP chair of suburban Cobb County. “The promise of the great Trump economy has not materialized."

Top Hill Republicans have worked behind the scenes for months to try to alleviate some of the political fallout from Trump’s election year policy moves, including arguing to White House officials that Maine Sen. Susan Collins and Michigan Senate nominee Mike Rogers could lose their races if the administration didn’t reach an off-ramp from the trade war with Canada, according to three Republicans with direct knowledge of the matter. Eventually, Trump agreed to roll back some tariffs and add new ones in a boost to Collins.

Republicans also pressed for the White House to undo some of Trump’s other controversial moves, like his executive order to import more foreign beef that has riled ranchers and farmers in red states like Kansas, Iowa and Texas. But that relief never came.

"Republicans have always been aware of the historical midterm precedent, and that's why we're barnstorming the country to tout the president's achievements on cutting taxes, securing the border, and lowering drug costs,” said Natalie Baldassarre, a spokesperson for the Republican National Committee. “Any anonymous strategist who says the president is not helpful in turning out Republican voters has no idea what they're talking about, and their candidates should request a refund for their shoddy consulting services."

But Trump’s actions, Republicans say, are hitting different parts of the country hard. The Iran war, they argue, was a significant blunder from Trump that has multiplied Democrats’ paths to power in both the House and Senate by driving fuel and fertilizer costs up — most notably impacting races across the Midwest.
The White House’s tariffs regime has been a major concern in battlegrounds on the Canadian border like Maine and Michigan.

Hardline immigration enforcement that has resulted in the deportation of thousands has hurt especially in heavily Latino border states like Arizona and Texas, and the cancelling of Temporary Protected Status for Haitians and Venezuelans has enraged South Florida voters. Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar, a Miami Republican, warned the president in a campaign ad earlier this year that his immigration tactics had gone too far.
“Trump won Miami, and yet he went to the place that gave him the biggest support, and kind of just fucked everybody over if we're being honest.” said one Florida-based Republican operative.
body_zh: 共和党人已经在私下指责唐纳德·特朗普总统，因为他们准备在周二遭受损失。
尽管他们竞相与他在关税、不受欢迎的伊朗战争和大规模驱逐议程方面的行动保持距离，但很少有人愿意公开批评他——这清楚地表明特朗普对共和党的控制力仍然有多么强大。但对大约十几名候选人、竞选官员和立法者的采访显示，他们非常清楚到底是谁在整个周期中让他们处于不利地位。
一位众议院共和党议员表示，“今年早些时候，我们真的觉得我们可以挑战历史。”他和本文中的其他人一样，被授予匿名权，可以坦诚地讨论中期动态。 “然后特朗普轰炸了伊朗。这就是一件又一件的事情。”
共和党在许多关键战场上的民意调查中都处于平局或落后状态，并预计会失去一些曾经稳固的红色席位。特朗普漫不经心的结束语——包括反复评论男性候选人的外貌——进一步让本已紧张的政党感到沮丧。
“我认为 Jon Husted 的屁股和 Nicki Minaj 的屁股是一个很棒的结束信息，”T.W.负责南卡罗来纳州参议员竞选的共和党策略师阿里吉等人在接受《与达莎·伯恩斯对话》采访时讽刺地说。 “你必须接受特朗普的好与坏，除非你每天都想把自己逼疯。”
“人们会追随总统。责任由他承担。他的支持率并不高，”他补充道。
私下里，一些共和党人甚至更加严厉。 “At least when Barack Obama was president, he only screwed his enemies, never his friends,” said a second House Republican.
白宫为其参与伊朗战争、关税制度和移民执法方式进行了辩护。白宫发言人戴维斯·英格尔在一份声明中表示，特朗普“是共和党明确的领导人、最好的使者和无与伦比的激励者，他致力于维持共和党在国会的多数席位。”
一位不愿透露姓名的白宫官员坦率地称这种指责游戏是“愚蠢的冒险”，并表示特朗普“显然把一切都留在了现场”。
如果共和党在周二跌入谷底，当特朗普接近其总统任期的跛脚鸭阶段时，指责他的悄悄话可能会演变成公开谴责，共和党人将重新关注如何在 2028 年重新赢得选民，并争夺自己在党内未来的席位。
“我不确定六个月后共和党会是什么样子。看，很多共和党人都保持沉默。许多对过去两年的发展方式有真正问题的共和党人都是好士兵，”一位参与全国竞争激烈的中期竞选的共和党策略师表示。 “但如果我们失去 35 个众议院席位和 6 个参议院席位，会发生什么？”
“我们都知道问题是谁。是特朗普。我们会继续走上失败的道路吗？”这位策略师补充道。
在佐治亚州，一些共和党人已经警告称，该州农村地区提前投票率低可能会拖累他们的全部选票。 “如果你住在佐治亚州农村，你会受到更高价格（尤其是柴油价格）的不成比例的伤害，”科布县郊区的前共和党主席贾森·谢泼德（Jason Shepherd）说。 “伟大的特朗普经济的承诺尚未实现。”
据三名直接了解此事的共和党人透露，数月来，顶级共和党人一直在幕后努力，试图减轻特朗普选举年政策举措带来的一些政治影响，包括向白宫官员辩称，如果政府不从与加拿大的贸易战中解脱出来，缅因州参议员苏珊·柯林斯和密歇根州参议院候选人迈克·罗杰斯可能会输掉竞选。最终，特朗普同意取消部分关税并增加新关税，以提振柯林斯。
共和党人还敦促白宫撤销特朗普的其他一些有争议的举措，例如他进口更多外国牛肉的行政命令，该命令激怒了堪萨斯州、爱荷华州和德克萨斯州等红色州的牧场主和农民。但这种解脱从未到来。
共和党全国委员会发言人娜塔莉·巴尔达萨尔表示：“共和党人一直都知道中期选举的历史先例，这就是为什么我们要在全国范围内宣传总统在减税、确保边境安全和降低药品成本方面取得的成就。” “任何声称总统无助于赢得共和党选民的匿名战略家都不知道他们在说什么，他们的候选人应该要求退款，因为他们的劣质咨询服务。”
但共和党人表示，特朗普的行动正在严重打击该国不同地区。他们认为，伊朗战争是特朗普的一个重大错误，导致燃料和化肥成本上升，从而增加了民主党在众议院和参议院掌权的途径，尤其是对中西部地区的竞选产生了影响。
白宫的关税制度一直是缅因州和密歇根州等加拿大边境战场的主要担忧。
强硬的移民执法导致数千人被驱逐出境，尤其是在亚利桑那州和德克萨斯州等拉丁裔边境州，取消海地人和委内瑞拉人的临时保护身份激怒了南佛罗里达州选民。迈阿密共和党众议员玛丽亚·埃尔维拉·萨拉查在今年早些时候的竞选广告中警告总统，他的移民策略太过分了。
“特朗普赢得了迈阿密，但他去了一个给了他最大支持的地方，如果我们说实话，那简直就是把所有人都搞砸了。”佛罗里达州的一名共和党特工说。

title_en: When it comes to election pressure, this year's Georgia or Michigan could be anywhere
title_zh: 说到选举压力，今年的佐治亚州或密歇根州可能是任何地方
summary: The districts that will decide control of the House and Senate next year are spread across the country. Voting officials in those places may face scrutiny and pressure they've never experienced.
summary_zh: 明年决定参众两院控制权的选区遍布全国。这些地方的投票官员可能面临审查
body_en: When it comes to election pressure, this year's Georgia or Michigan could be anywhere
There's one big difference, Tina Barton says, between running an election in a battleground state and a non-battleground.

"If a human error happens, it's easily explained in the press and it's not a story," Barton says. "You have a human error in a battleground state and all of a sudden it can become a massive conspiracy."

In 2020, she oversaw elections as city clerk of Rochester Hills, Mich. On election night, her office mistakenly sent an unofficial absentee vote file twice because the first one didn't initially appear to send.
Justice Department issues subpoenas to California election workers

Such mistakes happen every election cycle in a national process run by tens of thousands of human beings. A machine isn't plugged in. A poll worker sleeps through their alarm clock and doesn't open a precinct on time. Someone gets handed the wrong ballot.
In Barton's case, the issue didn't impact actual votes, and it was corrected in the tally the following day.

The chairwoman of the Republican National Committee accused her office of improperly giving votes to Democrats, and Barton received a rush of death threats, including a voicemail saying she deserved a "throat to the knife" because she had "frauded out America of a real election."
More than half a decade later, for better or worse, election officials in swing states like Michigan, Georgia and Arizona are more used to that level of pressure and scrutiny.

In this year's midterms, however, because the races that will decide control of the U.S. House and Senate are spread around the country, local officials in places like Iowa, Alaska, New York and Kansas may find themselves in the national spotlight for the first time.
The Justice Department begins notifying counties where it wants to monitor elections

Chris McGinn is executive director of the Texas Association of County Election Officials. In an interview with NPR earlier this year, he noted that Texas has been a reliable Republican state for the better part of 50 years , which has meant fewer competitive elections and less pressure on voting officials in federal election cycles.

A huge part of McGinn's job has been preparing clerks for the possibility that could change this year, considering the U.S. Senate race there could decide the balance of power in that chamber. The Republican nominee for that seat sought to help President Trump overturn his 2020 election loss.

"We're still in a state of not thinking it can happen to us — 'That happens in other places,'" McGinn said. "One of the things that I jokingly but realistically preach to our members is we don't want to be Florida in 2000."
On a whole, the threat environment for voting officials seems calmer than it did in the period following 2020.

Wendy Link — the supervisor of elections for Palm Beach County, Fla., a county that includes part of a toss-up congressional district this year — says her office still regularly gets "love letters," as she calls them, but she's not as worried for own safety as she has been at different points in the job.

"We get emails saying, you know, 'We're going to send our army to arrest you, you'll be spending your time in Guantanamo Bay,'" Link told NPR. "So do I love reading some of the emails? No. Do I think some of them are clearly intended to intimidate me? Yes. But am I reaching out and asking for a security detail? No."
The real reason it's going to take a while to know who won in some midterm races

But Barton, the former Michigan clerk, worries it could all escalate again if the midterms are close. She's now vice president of the Committee for Safe and Secure Elections, which helps local officials game-plan and prepare for different worst case scenarios.

"It can happen whether you're a red state or a blue state. Controversy can find you," Barton said. "All it takes is some ballot equipment going down, a problem with ballots jamming, a website going down."
body_zh: 说到选举压力，今年的佐治亚州或密歇根州可能是任何地方
蒂娜·巴顿说，在战场州和非战场州进行选举有一个很大的区别。
“如果发生人为错误，很容易在媒体上解释，这不是一个故事，”巴顿说。 “在战场状态下出现人为错误，突然间它可能会变成一个巨大的阴谋。”
2020 年，她作为密歇根州罗切斯特山市的市书记员负责监督选举。在选举之夜，她的办公室两次错误地发送了非官方缺席投票文件，因为第一个文件最初似乎并未发送。
司法部向加州选举工作人员发出传票
在由数万人主导的国家进程中，这样的错误在每个选举周期都会发生。机器没有插上电源。一名投票工作人员在闹钟响之前一直在睡觉，没有准时开放选区。有人收到了错误的选票。
就巴顿而言，该问题并未影响实际投票，并在第二天的计票中得到纠正。
共和党全国委员会主席指责她的办公室不恰当地为民主党投票，巴顿收到了大量死亡威胁，其中包括一封语音邮件，称她应该“被刀割断”，因为她“欺骗了美国进行真正的选举”。
五年多后，无论好坏，密歇根州、佐治亚州和亚利桑那州等摇摆州的选举官员都已经习惯了这种程度的压力和审查。
然而，在今年的中期选举中，由于决定美国参众两院控制权的竞选分散在全国各地，爱荷华州、阿拉斯加州、纽约州和堪萨斯州等地的地方官员可能会首次成为全国关注的焦点。
司法部开始通知希望监督选举的县
克里斯·麦金 (Chris McGinn) 是德克萨斯州县选举官员协会的执行董事。在今年早些时候接受 NPR 采访时，他指出，50 年来的大部分时间里，德克萨斯州一直是一个可靠的共和党州，这意味着竞争性选举减少，联邦选举周期中投票官员面临的压力也更小。
考虑到美国参议院的竞选可能决定参议院的权力平衡，麦金的大部分工作就是让职员为今年可能发生的变化做好准备。该席位的共和党提名人试图帮助特朗普总统扭转 2020 年选举的失利。
麦金说：“我们仍然认为这种事不会发生在我们身上——‘这种事发生在其他地方’。” “我开玩笑但实事求是地向我们的会员宣讲的一件事是，我们不想成为 2000 年的佛罗里达。”
总体而言，投票官员面临的威胁环境似乎比 2020 年之后的时期更加平静。
佛罗里达州棕榈滩县的选举主管温迪·林克(Wendy Link)表示，她的办公室仍然经常收到她所说的“情书”，但她并不像工作中的其他阶段那样担心自己的安全。今年，该县包括了一个不稳定的国会选区。
“我们收到电子邮件说，你知道，‘我们将派出我们的军队来逮捕你，你将在关塔那摩湾度过你的时光，’”林克告诉美国公共广播电台。 “那么我喜欢阅读其中一些电子邮件吗？不。我是否认为其中一些邮件明显是为了恐吓我？是的。但我是否主动联系并询问安全细节？不。”
需要一段时间才能知道谁在一些中期选举中获胜的真正原因
但前密歇根州职员巴顿担心，如果中期选举临近，事情可能会再次升级。她现在是安全选举委员会的副主席，该委员会帮助地方官员制定计划并为不同的最坏情况做好准备。
“无论你是红州还是蓝州，这种情况都可能发生。争议会找到你，”巴顿说。 “所需要的只是一些投票设备出现故障、选票堵塞问题、网站出现故障。”

title_en: 6 things to watch for on election night
title_zh: 选举之夜需要注意的 6 件事
summary: Some of the key storylines to watch will center around various voters groups that have soured on President Trump during his second turn out.
summary_zh: 一些值得关注的关键故事情节将围绕在特朗普总统第二次投票期间对他产生不满的各个选民群体展开。
body_en: People walk by a sign for voting on November 1, 2026, in Detroit, Michigan. Michigan has become a focal point in the upcoming midterm elections, with a close race between Republican Senate candidate, former U.S. Rep. Mike Rogers (R-MI), and Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed that could decide who controls the chamber. Spencer Platt/Getty Images hide caption

It can be hard to know what to focus on in midterm elections. There are so many races, from elections for governor and senator to the House and state legislatures. For a better idea of how the night might go to see which party might control Congress, here are six things to watch
1. The early bellwethers for Republican turnout and the Latino vote

There are two states, Indiana and Kentucky, that will see results in the 6 p.m. ET hour. And then there's Florida, which is split between the Eastern and Central time zones. But most of the state is on Eastern time. So lots of House race results will be coming in during the 7 p.m. ET hour, even if statewide contests like the Senate and governors races won't be called at the earliest until 8 p.m. ET.

Some races to watch for early indicators of what might come later in the evening — Indiana's 5th Congressional District, Kentucky's 6th and Florida's 22nd and 27th. Indiana's 5th and Kentucky's 6th are seats held by Republicans that are more competitive now than at the beginning of the cycle. If these are close or tipping to Democrats, it could be a sign of low Republican turnout and a bigger Democratic wave.

Florida's 22nd is held by a Democrat but redrawn to tip in Republicans' favor. Trump won Florida's 27th by double-digits so this heavily Latino district could be an indicator of how this key subgroup votes.
Independents are a key swing group, but they are also a lower-propensity voting group in midterms.

It used to be that Republicans had to win a bigger share of independents before the Trump era. Mitt Romney, for example, won 55% of independents in 2012 but lost the presidential election. But there's been a political realignment in this country with blue-collar white voters trending toward Trump, fewer people identifying as Democrats and better-educated white voters shifting toward Democrats.
So in the decade since Trump has been on the political scene, Republicans have done well when they win at least 46% of independents. When they haven't, they've lost.

The Michigan Senate race is important for control of the Senate. If Republicans flip it, the magic number for Democrats goes from four to five, meaning Democrats would have to win five seats held by Republicans to win control of the Senate.

For Abdul El-Sayed (D) to win in Michigan, a key is going to be Black voters in Wayne County. If he runs up the score in and around Detroit, he has a path to victory, but if he doesn't, it becomes that much harder — and it's been an area of vulnerability for him.
During the Trump era, Democrats have needed 68% or more in Wayne County to win Michigan unless, like Sen. Elissa Slotkin in 2024, they can overperform in the suburbs.

Voters 18 to 29 see a drastic drop off in turnout between presidential and midterm elections. During presidential races since 1992, 43% of registered young voters cast ballots. But in midterms, that falls to 21%, just 1 in 5 who show up at the polls.

But they are crucial to Democratic success. In the last 20 years, when Democrats won this group by more than 20 points, they have done well, winning presidencies or making gains in midterms. The only exception was 2022, but arguably, the strong margin Democrats won with young voters that year, helped them stem what could have been a much larger Republican tide. That year, Democrats lost nine House seats, but gained a Senate seat.
Democratic margin with voters 18-29, election result
2022 +28, Republicans win House, Democrats gain Senate seat
2014 +11, Republicans expand House majority, win Senate
5. In Texas, the keys will be the difference between Gov. Greg Abbott (R) and Ken Paxton's (R) vote totals – and the Latino vote in South Texas
Given past polling errors in Texas that underestimated the Republican vote, there's a healthy skepticism that Democrat James Talarico's margin of error lead in polling averages is enough to win.

There was lots of enthusiasm in 2018 for Beto O'Rourke's (D) 2018 bid against an unpopular Republican senator in Ted Cruz, but Cruz still won, although by less than 3 percentage points. No Democrat has won statewide in Texas since 1994, and no Democrat has been elected to the Senate from Texas in 38 years.
body_zh: 2026 年 11 月 1 日，在密歇根州底特律，人们走过投票标志。密歇根州已成为即将到来的中期选举的焦点，共和党参议院候选人、前美国众议员迈克·罗杰斯 (R-MI) 和民主党候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德之间的激烈竞争可能会决定谁控制参议院。斯宾塞普拉特/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
很难知道中期选举应该关注什么。有很多竞选活动，从州长和参议员的选举到众议院和州立法机构的选举。为了更好地了解今晚将如何进行，看看哪个政党可能会控制国会，以下是值得关注的六件事
1. 共和党投票率和拉丁裔选票的早期风向标
印第安纳州和肯塔基州这两个州将于下午 6 点看到结果。东部时间。然后是佛罗里达州，分为东部时区和中部时区。但该州大部分地区采用东部时间。因此，许多众议院比赛的结果将在晚上 7 点公布。东部时间，即使参议院和州长竞选等全州范围的竞选最早要到晚上 8 点才会举行。等。
一些比赛需要留意今晚晚些时候可能发生的比赛的早期迹象——印第安纳州第 5 届国会选区、肯塔基州第 6 届以及佛罗里达州第 22 届和第 27 届国会选区。印第安纳州的第五个席位和肯塔基州的第六个席位由共和党占据，现在比周期开始时更具竞争力。如果这些结果接近或倾向于民主党，这可能表明共和党投票率较低，民主党浪潮更大。
佛罗里达州第 22 届选举由民主党人举行，但重新选举结果有利于共和党人。特朗普以两位数的优势赢得了佛罗里达州的第 27 票，因此这个拉丁裔人口众多的选区可能会成为衡量这一关键群体投票情况的一个指标。
独立人士是一个关键的摇摆群体，但他们也是中期选举中投票倾向较低的群体。
在特朗普时代之前，共和党必须赢得更大比例的独立人士。例如，米特·罗姆尼 (Mitt Romney) 在 2012 年赢得了 55% 的独立人士支持，但在总统选举中落败。但这个国家正在发生政治重组，蓝领白人选民倾向于特朗普，自认为民主党的人越来越少，而受过良好教育的白人选民则转向民主党。
因此，自特朗普登上政坛以来的十年里，共和党赢得了至少 46% 的无党派人士支持，就已经表现不错了。当他们没有做到的时候，他们就输了。
密歇根州参议员竞选对于参议院的控制权很重要。如果共和党翻转它，民主党的神奇数字将从四个增加到五个，这意味着民主党必须赢得共和党占据的五个席位才能赢得参议院的控制权。
阿卜杜勒·赛义德（民主党）要想在密歇根州获胜，关键是韦恩县的黑人选民。如果他在底特律及其周边地区得分，他就有一条通往胜利的道路，但如果他没有，那就变得更加困难——这对他来说是一个脆弱的领域。
在特朗普时代，民主党需要在韦恩县获得 68% 或更多的选票才能赢得密歇根州，除非他们能像 2024 年的参议员埃丽莎·斯洛特金 (Elissa Slotkin) 那样在郊区表现出色。
18 岁至 29 岁的选民认为，总统选举和中期选举之间的投票率急剧下降。自1992年以来的总统竞选中，43%的登记年轻选民参加了投票。但到了中期选举，这一比例下降至 21%，即只有五分之一的人参加了民意调查。
但它们对于民主党的成功至关重要。过去20年里，当民主党以超过20个百分点的优势赢得这一组时，他们已经做得很好，赢得了总统职位或在中期选举中取得了进展。唯一的例外是 2022 年，但可以说，当年民主党在年轻选民中赢得了巨大优势，帮助他们阻止了可能规模更大的共和党浪潮。那一年，民主党失去了九个众议院席位，但获得了一个参议院席位。
选举结果，民主党以 18 比 29 的优势领先选民
2022+28，共和党赢得众议院，民主党获得参议院席位
2014 +11，共和党扩大众议院多数席位，赢得参议院
5. 在德克萨斯州，关键将是州长格雷格·阿博特（R）和肯·帕克斯顿（R）的选票总数之间的差异，以及德克萨斯州南部的拉丁裔选票
鉴于德克萨斯州过去的民意调查错误低估了共和党的选票，人们对民主党詹姆斯·塔拉里科(James Talarico)在民意调查平均值上的误差幅度领先是否足以获胜存在合理的怀疑。
2018 年，人们对贝托·奥罗克 (D) 2018 年竞选与不受欢迎的共和党参议员特德·克鲁兹 (Ted Cruz) 的竞争抱有很大热情，但克鲁兹仍然获胜，尽管领先幅度不到 3 个百分点。自 1994 年以来，还没有民主党人在德克萨斯州赢得全州选举，38 年来也没有民主党人当选德克萨斯州参议员。

body_en: Washington state resident dies from ‘severe illness’ after contracting bird flu | Washington state
Washington state resident dies from ‘severe illness’ after contracting bird flu
Individual, who also had underlying conditions, was hospitalized after being exposed to avian influenza
A Washington state resident has died after being hospitalized with “severe illness” after contracting bird flu, local health officials said on Sunday.

The individual was exposed to avian influenza, also known as bird flu, at a dairy with infected cattle in Yakima county, according to a news release . The person was subsequently hospitalized with severe illness and died on Sunday. Health officials said that the individual, whose identity had not been released, had underlying health conditions.
“The Yakima health district offers its heartfelt condolences to the individual’s family, friends, and loved ones during this difficult time,” the district said in a statement.

This is the first person in the United States to die from complications from bird flu this year, according to the Associated Press . It comes as officials in Yakima county have reported that since early October , 33 dairy herds have tested positive for “highly pathogenic avian influenza”.
‘It’s clear they are under-vaccinated’: Amish under spotlight amid Pennsylvania measles outbreak

The Yakima health district has said that it, in coordination with the Washington state department of health, is monitoring human cases of bird flu in Yakima county. So far, the district has recorded three confirmed human cases in the county.

In Sunday’s statement, the health district announced the county’s third confirmed human case of bird flu. The individual was “exposed to infected dairy cattle at a Yakima county dairy”, but has not experienced severe illness or required hospitalization.
Officials said they are working with public health partners to identify and contact any individuals “who may have been in close contact with the person to monitor for symptoms”.

County officials have stressed that “the risk of avian influenza infection to the general public remains low” and that “people at greater risk include dairy workers and others who have close or prolonged contact with infected animals or environments contaminated with the virus”.
Human-to-human transmission of bird flu is “extremely rare and has never been documented in the United States”, they said.

The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has recorded 72 human cases of bird flu across the country since 2024, according to agency data. The CDC has maintained that there is no known person-to-person spread and that the risk to the general public remains low.
The CDC announced the first death in the US due to complications from bird flu in January 2025.
body_zh: 华盛顿州居民感染禽流感后死于“重病”华盛顿州
华盛顿州居民感染禽流感后死于“重病”
个人也有基础疾病，在接触禽流感后被送往医院
当地卫生官员周日表示，一名华盛顿州居民因感染禽流感而“重病”住院后死亡。
据新闻稿称，该人在亚基马县一家饲养受感染牛的奶牛场接触了禽流感，也称为禽流感。该人随后因病情严重入院治疗，并于周日去世。卫生官员表示，该人的身份尚未公布，但他有潜在的健康问题。
该地区在一份声明中表示：“在这个困难时期，亚基马卫生区向患者的家人、朋友和亲人表示衷心的慰问。”
据美联社报道，这是美国今年第一例死于禽流感并发症的人。据亚基马县官员报告，自10月初以来，已有33个奶牛群检测出“高致病性禽流感”呈阳性。
“很明显他们没有接种疫苗”：宾夕法尼亚州麻疹疫情中阿米什人受到关注
亚基马卫生区表示，它正在与华盛顿州卫生部协调，监测亚基马县的人类禽流感病例。截至目前，该县已报告三起人间确诊病例。
在周日的声明中，卫生区宣布了该县第三例确诊的人感染禽流感病例。该人“在亚基马县的一家奶牛场接触过受感染的奶牛”，但没有出现严重疾病或需要住院治疗。
官员们表示，他们正在与公共卫生合作伙伴合作，以识别并联系任何“可能与该人有过密切接触的人，以监测症状”。
县官员强调，“公众感染禽流感的风险仍然很低”，“风险较大的人包括乳制品工人和其他与受感染动物或受病毒污染的环境有密切或长期接触的人”。
他们说，禽流感的人际传播“极其罕见，在美国从未有过记录”。
据机构数据显示，自 2024 年以来，美国疾病控制与预防中心 (CDC) 已在全国记录了 72 例人感染禽流感病例。疾病预防控制中心坚称，不存在已知的人际传播情况，公众面临的风险仍然很低。
CDC 于 2025 年 1 月宣布美国首例因禽流感并发症死亡的病例。

body_en: Young co-pilot, 20, named as one of nine victims of deadly Florida plane crash
Family of four, two close friends and nanny also died in crash as pilot identified as 55-year-old Jeff Gregory
Family members on Monday identified a young Florida pilot as one of nine victims of a plane crash in Palm Beach county that occurred during a heavy thunderstorm.

Nathalia Filgueiras, 20, was co-pilot of the private Learjet 60 en route from Austin-Bergstrom international airport in Texas to North Eleuthera airport in the Bahamas on Sunday when it suddenly plummeted out of the sky, killing all onboard, her mother told the New York Times .
Later on Monday, the family of the passengers who died posted a statement on Facebook identifying the victims and paying tribute to them.

It named them as Adam Robinson, 45, a Texas-based technology entrepreneur; his wife Helen Sharp, 40; and their children, Emma, four, and Charlie, two. The statement said close family friends Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr were also killed, along with Anita Maria Cetina, the children’s nanny.
The pilot in charge of the Learjet was identified by TMZ and other media outlets on Monday as Jeff Gregory, 55, an experienced aviator from Pennsylvania.

The plane crashed at 12.51pm local time on Sunday, exploding on impact, leaving a giant crater in the ground, and scattering debris all around the crash site near a mobile home park in the city of Greenacres.

At a briefing on Monday, Tom Chapman, head of a team of about 20 National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) personnel in West Palm Beach, said conditions in south Florida on Sunday were “pretty crazy”, and that the weather would be “a major focus” of the investigation.
“You all saw what the weather was like here at the surface. What we have to determine is what the weather conditions were like at altitude,” he said.

Filgueiras’s mother, Camila Corteleti, told the Times her daughter worked for Upper Jets, a private charter firm based in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, which owned the aircraft, and that she had been passionate about flying since childhood.
“She loved the freedom. It was completely different seeing the world from the top,” Cortelini said, adding that her daughter enjoyed plane spotting at local airports as a young girl.
Filgueiras graduated high school in Boca Raton, Florida, in 2024, having already obtained her private pilot’s license at the age of 17, according to the Palm Beach CBS affiliate 12 News .
Aurora Aviation, which operated the aircraft under its trading name of Upper Jets, did not respond to a request for comment.
Robinson was the founder of several technology companies, and his wife owned a public relations firm, according to relatives.
“Adam and Helen were devoted parents, and Emma and Charlie were the light of their lives,” the statement said.

“Helen and Adam were the love affair that will last for ever. Their warmth, generosity and gift for making people feel welcome touched so many lives. Their loss will be felt deeply by all those who loved them and who they loved in return.

“Charmi and Rachel were full of joy and adventure. They loved their people fiercely, fully and without hesitation. From the moment they met, they were all in on each other and the life they were building. They are deeply loved, and we will miss them endlessly.
“Anita Maria cared for Emma and Charlie with tenderness and devotion, and she was truly part of the family. She showed us a legacy of unconditional love and devotion.”

Chapman of the NTSB said at the press conference: “I want to express our profound, profound condolences to the family and friends of those who were lost in this tragedy. We are truly, truly sorry for your loss.”
body_zh: 20 岁的年轻副驾驶被列为佛罗里达州致命空难的九名遇难者之一
一家四口、两名密友和保姆也​​在坠机事故中丧生，飞行员被确认为 55 岁的杰夫·格雷戈里 (Jeff Gregory)
周一，家人确认一名年轻的佛罗里达飞行员是棕榈滩县一场猛烈雷暴期间发生的飞机失事的九名遇难者之一。
20 岁的娜塔莉亚·菲尔盖拉斯 (Nathalia Filgueiras) 的母亲告诉《纽约时报》，她是里尔 60 型私人飞机的副驾驶，周日，这架飞机从德克萨斯州奥斯汀-博格斯多姆国际机场飞往巴哈马的北伊柳塞拉机场，飞机突然从天而降，机上人员全部遇难。
周一晚些时候，遇难乘客家属在脸书上发布声明，确认遇难者身份并向他们表示哀悼。
他们的名字是 Adam Robinson，45 岁，德克萨斯州科技企业家；他的妻子海伦·夏普，40 岁；以及他们的孩子，四岁的艾玛和两岁的查理。声明称，家庭好友瑞秋·里德 (Rachael Reed) 和查米·费尔 (Charmi Fehr) 以及孩子们的保姆安妮塔·玛丽亚·塞蒂娜 (Anita Maria Cetina) 也被杀害。
TMZ 和其他媒体周一确认，负责这架里尔喷气式飞机的飞行员是杰夫·格雷戈里 (Jeff Gregory)，55 岁，来自宾夕法尼亚州，是一位经验丰富的飞行员。
这架飞机于当地时间周日中午 12 点 51 分坠毁，撞击后爆炸，地面留下一个巨大的弹坑，碎片散落在格林埃克斯市一个移动房屋公园附近的坠机地点周围。
在周一的新闻发布会上，西棕榈滩约 20 名国家运输安全委员会 (NTSB) 人员组成的团队负责人汤姆·查普曼 (Tom Chapman) 表示，周日佛罗里达州南部的情况“相当疯狂”，天气将成为调查的“主要焦点”。
“你们都看到了地表的天气状况。我们必须确定的是高空的天气状况，”他说。
菲尔盖拉斯的母亲卡米拉·科特莱蒂 (Camila Corteleti) 告诉《泰晤士报》，她的女儿在位于佛罗里达州劳德代尔堡的私人包机公司 Upper Jets 工作，该公司拥有这架飞机，她从小就热衷于飞行。
“她热爱自由。从高处看世界是完全不同的，”科泰利尼说，并补充说，她的女儿小时候很喜欢在当地机场观看飞机。
据哥伦比亚广播公司棕榈滩附属机构 12 News 报道，菲尔盖拉斯于 2024 年在佛罗里达州博卡拉顿高中毕业，17 岁时就已经获得了私人飞行员执照。
奥罗拉航空公司（Aurora Aviation）以其商业名称Upper Jets运营这架飞机，没有回应置评请求。
据亲戚称，罗宾逊是多家科技公司的创始人，他的妻子拥有一家公关公司。
声明称：“亚当和海伦是忠诚的父母，艾玛和查理是他们生命中的光明。”
“海伦和亚当的爱情将永远持续下去。他们的热情、慷慨和让人们感到受欢迎的天赋感动了许多人。所有爱他们的人和他们所爱的人都将深深地感受到他们的离去。
“查米和瑞秋充满了欢乐和冒险精神。他们热烈、全心全意、毫不犹豫地爱着自己的人民。从他们相遇的那一刻起，他们就全心全意地投入到彼此以及他们正在建设的生活中。他们被深深地爱着，我们将永远怀念他们。
“安妮塔·玛丽亚温柔而忠诚地照顾艾玛和查理，她是这个家庭真正的一部分。她向我们展示了无条件的爱和奉献精神。”
美国国家运输安全委员会的查普曼在新闻发布会上表示：“我想向这场悲剧中遇难者的家人和朋友表示深切的哀悼。对于你们的损失，我们深感抱歉。”

title_en: Lindsay Clancy back in court seeking to dismiss murder charges after mistrial
title_zh: 林赛·克兰西重回法庭，寻求在审判失败后驳回谋杀指控
summary: Lawyers for Massachusetts mother who killed children argue new trial would violate double jeopardy rules Lindsay Clancy returned to court on Monday in an attempt to dismiss the charges that she murdered her three young children. The hearing Monday was the seco
summary_zh: 马萨诸塞州杀害儿童母亲的律师辩称，新的审判将违反双重危险规则。林赛·克兰西周一返回法庭。
body_en: Lindsay Clancy back in court seeking to dismiss murder charges after mistrial
Lawyers for Massachusetts mother who killed children argue new trial would violate double jeopardy rules
Lindsay Clancy returned to court on Monday in an attempt to dismiss the charges that she murdered her three young children.
The hearing Monday was the second time the Massachusetts mother has been in court since her trial ended with a deadlocked jury in September after jurors were unable to agree on a verdict.

Clancy has never disputed killing her three young children in 2023, but her lawyer has argued she had postpartum psychosis and was unable to control her behavior. Prosecutors have acknowledged that the 36-year-old Clancy had mental health problems but said she acted deliberately and understood her actions were wrong.
The focus of the hearing in front of Judge William Sullivan was a motion from the defense to dismiss the charges on double jeopardy grounds.
Lindsay Clancy judge declares mistrial – what happens next?

At Monday’s hearing, defense attorney Martin G Weinberg argued that Sullivan should have investigated further after the jury foreperson sent two notes indicating that a juror was not following the rules. Further questioning could have revealed grounds to remove the lone holdout juror, Michael Desronvil, and continue deliberations – potentially avoiding the mistrial, he said.
Kevin Reddington, another attorney representing Clancy, urged the court to examine Desronvil’s juror questionnaire, alleging that he had been dishonest in his responses.
Reddington also said he had evidence that Desronvil used his phone during deliberations and he allegedly researched altruistic filicide, USA Today reports.
Upon using Desronvil’s name, Sullivan said: “I’m going to stop you right there,” to which Reddington responded: “No, you’re not going to stop me.”
Sullivan went on to say that there was “no need here in this courtroom to use that” juror’s name, according to the Boston Globe.
In response, Reddington said: “He’s got more face time than I do,” appearing to refer to Desronvil’s media appearances following the trial.
Reddington also urged the court to determine whether Desronvil had conducted any research related to the trial, which could have warranted his dismissal.
Jennifer Sprague, a Plymouth county assistant district attorney, pushed back, saying: “If the door is open to examining this juror, it would be open on all jurors,” the New York Times reports .

After receiving the notes, Sullivan spoke with each juror, reminded them of their duties and explained what constitutes reasonable doubt. He asked whether they could apply the law to the case, and all said yes.

But Weinberg argued that Sullivan had not gone far enough. A juror who said he could follow the law could have been lying, Weinberg said, and the situation warranted questioning the foreperson separately to learn more about what was happening during deliberations.
“That’s what the foreperson was asking the court to do,” Weinberg said. “I can see that this is not easy,” he told the judge at one point.
“You don’t have to keep saying that – I have thick skin,” Sullivan replied.

Prosecutor Jennifer Sprague argued that Sullivan had struck the right balance in his handling of the jury. Pressing the foreperson further would have required delving into the substance of the jury’s deliberations, potentially inserting the court’s “interpretation of what is correct” into the process.
body_zh: 林赛·克兰西重回法庭，寻求在审判失败后驳回谋杀指控
马萨诸塞州杀害儿童母亲的律师辩称，新的审判将违反双重危险规则
林赛·克兰西周一重返法庭，试图驳回对她谋杀三个孩子的指控。
周一的听证会是这位马萨诸塞州母亲自去年 9 月因陪审团无法就判决达成一致而导致陪审团陷入僵局以来第二次出庭。
克兰西从未对 2023 年杀死她的三个孩子提出异议，但她的律师辩称她患有产后精神病，无法控制自己的行为。检察官承认 36 岁的克兰西有精神健康问题，但表示她是故意行为，并明白自己的行为是错误的。
法官威廉·沙利文 (William Sullivan) 听证会的焦点是辩方提出的以双重危险为由驳回指控的动议。
林赛·克兰西法官宣布审判无效——接下来会发生什么？
在周一的听证会上，辩护律师马丁·G·温伯格 (Martin G Weinberg) 辩称，在陪审团主席发送了两份说明表明陪审员没有遵守规则后，沙利文应该进一步调查。他说，进一步的质询可能会揭示出罢免唯一坚持不懈的陪审员迈克尔·德斯隆维尔(Michael Desronvil)的理由，并继续审议——有可能避免审判无效。
克兰西的另一位代理律师凯文·雷丁顿敦促法庭检查德斯隆维尔的陪审员调查问卷，声称他的回答不诚实。
据《今日美国》报道，雷丁顿还表示，他有证据表明德斯隆维尔在审议期间使用了他的手机，并且据称他研究了利他杀子行为。
在使用德斯隆维尔的名字时，沙利文说：“我会在那里阻止你，”雷丁顿回答道：“不，你不会阻止我。”
据《波士顿环球报》报道，沙利文接着表示，“在这个法庭上没有必要使用那个”陪审员的名字。
作为回应，雷丁顿说：“他比我有更多的见面时间”，这似乎指的是德斯隆维尔在审判后出现在媒体上的情况。
雷丁顿还敦促法院确定德斯隆维尔是否进行了与审判相关的任何研究，这可能有理由解雇他。
据《纽约时报》报道，普利茅斯县助理地方检察官詹妮弗·斯普拉格反驳说：“如果审查这位陪审员的大门是敞开的，那么它也会向所有陪审员敞开。”
收到笔记后，沙利文与每位陪审员进行了交谈，提醒他们自己的职责，并解释了什么构成合理怀疑。他询问是否可以适用法律来处理此案，大家都说可以。
但温伯格认为沙利文做得还不够。温伯格说，一个说自己可以遵守法律的陪审员可能是在撒谎，这种情况有必要单独向首席法官询问，以更多地了解审议过程中发生的情况。
“这就是工头要求法庭做的事情，”温伯格说。 “我知道这并不容易，”他一度告诉法官。
“你不必一直这么说——我脸皮很厚，”沙利文回答道。
检察官詹妮弗·斯普拉格辩称，沙利文在处理陪审团问题上取得了正确的平衡。进一步向领班人施压需要深入研究陪审团审议的实质内容，有可能将法院的“对正确的解释”插入到整个过程中。

title_en: Trump pre-election pitch: Reflecting Pool, pipes and a new promenade
title_zh: 特朗普选前宣传：倒影池、管道和新长廊
summary: President Trump extolled his administration's Reflecting Pool project , dug up debunked claims of vandalism and applauded the new White House helipad in a Monday pre-Election Day speech. The big picture: Trump's deep focus on remaking the nation's capital has
summary_zh: 特朗普总统赞扬了他的政府的倒影池项目，揭露了被揭穿的破坏行为指控，并对新的白宫直升机停机坪表示赞赏
body_en: President Trump extolled his administration's Reflecting Pool project , dug up debunked claims of vandalism and applauded the new White House helipad in a Monday pre-Election Day speech.
The big picture: Trump's deep focus on remaking the nation's capital has taken center stage as the clock ticks down to midterm elections.
Driving the news: "The pool is now better and more beautiful than it's ever been before, and we're very proud of it," Trump said in Monday's speech, adding, "We went through a lot with vandalism."

But Trump's own Justice Department dropped vandalism charges against former Olympian David Hearn , whose case was later killed by a judge after prosecutors acknowledged that faulty installation caused the damage to the Pool.
Trump added the administration was "giving serious thought" to renaming the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool to the "Trump Reflecting Pool," before later saying he was kidding.

Throughout the speech, he held up printed images he identified as pipes, joints and other Pool materials. He also showed an image that appeared to show "8647" sprayed onto the base of the emptied pool, claiming "that was a Comey phrase" — a reference to his former FBI director and top foe.
Zoom out: He also discussed his White House renovation projects, including the recently installed helipad and Scotts Miracle-Gro's lawn restoration after the UFC fight on White House grounds.
Friction point: Trump's projects, including his D.C.-area arch and White House ballroom, have been broadly panned by Americans in polling.
"This project should be a project that unites all Americans," Trump said Monday of the newly reopened Reflecting Pool, which stood empty for an extended period earlier this year.
Zoom in: His pre-election pitch at times sounded more like a typical rally speech, where he touted his immigration policies and war with Iran while slamming Democrats as "a party that hates America."

This is the last day before the midterm elections, the most important midterm I believe in our lifetime," he said. "The Democrat Party has nominated the most extreme and dangerous slate of candidates in American history."
He also reiterated his pitch to distribute $5,000 checks should Republicans win in the midterms.

What's next: After inviting Interior Secretary Doug Burgum to speak, Trump then touted his planned " triumphal arch ," detailed plans for a "promenade" from the Lincoln Memorial to the Potomac River and teased his golf course renovation .
"We have a lot of great things planned for Washington, and I could get into the nation, but for that you don't have enough time," Trump said.

He ended his closing argument by lauding a "golden age," saying, "We were laughed at like we were stupid people. We were laughed at by every ruler, every president, every prime minister, every king, every queen. But they don't laugh anymore."
Axios' Josephine Walker contributed to this report.

body_zh: 特朗普总统在周一选举日前的演讲中赞扬了他的政府的倒影池项目，揭露了被揭穿的破坏行为指控，并对新的白宫直升机停机坪表示赞赏。
总体情况：随着中期选举的临近，特朗普对重建国家首都的高度关注已成为焦点。
推动新闻：“现在的游泳池比以前更好、更漂亮，我们对此感到非常自豪，”特朗普在周一的演讲中说道，并补充道，“我们经历了很多破坏行为。”
但特朗普自己的司法部撤销了对前奥运选手大卫·赫恩的破坏公物指控，在检察官承认错误的安装导致泳池受损后，法官随后驳回了他的案件。
特朗普补充说，政府正在“认真考虑”将林肯纪念堂倒影池重新命名为“特朗普倒影池”，后来又说他是在开玩笑。
在整个演讲过程中，他一直举着印刷图像，他认为这些图像是管道、接头和其他泳池材料。他还展示了一张似乎显示“8647”喷在空池底部的图片，声称“这是科米的短语”——指的是他的前联邦调查局局长和头号敌人。
缩小：他还讨论了他的白宫改造项目，包括最近安装的直升机停机坪和 UFC 在白宫场地举行比赛后修复 Scotts Miracle-Gro 的草坪。
摩擦点：特朗普的项目，包括他的华盛顿地区拱门和白宫宴会厅，在民意调查中受到了美国人的广泛批评。
“这个项目应该是一个团结所有美国人的项目，”特朗普周一在谈到今年早些时候重新开放的倒影池时表示，该池在今年早些时候长期空置。
放大：他的选前演讲有时听起来更像是一场典型的集会演讲，他在演讲中宣扬自己的移民政策和与伊朗的战争，同时抨击民主党是“仇恨美国的政党”。
这是中期选举前的最后一天，我相信这是我们一生中最重要的中期选举，”他说。“民主党提名了美国历史上最极端、最危险的候选人名单。”
他还重申，如果共和党在中期选举中获胜，他将分发 5,000 美元的支票。
接下来：在邀请内政部长道格·布尔古姆发言后，特朗普吹捧了他计划中的“凯旋门”，详细介绍了从林肯纪念堂到波托马克河的“长廊”计划，并嘲笑了他的高尔夫球场翻新工程。
特朗普说：“我们为华盛顿计划了很多伟大的事情，我可以进入这个国家，但你没有足够的时间。”
他在结案陈词中赞扬了“黄金时代”，他说：“我们被嘲笑，就像我们是愚蠢的人一样。每一位统治者、每一位总统、每一位总理、每一位国王、每一位女王都嘲笑我们。但他们不再笑了。”
Axios 的 Josephine Walker 对本报告做出了贡献。
