title_en: AI chatbots are becoming political advisers. Their answers can mislead voters
title_zh: 人工智能聊天机器人正在成为政治顾问。他们的答案可能会误导选民
summary: Millions of Americans are turning to AI for election information, but chatbots are getting voting facts wrong and recommending candidates, raising concerns they could influence voters' decisions.
summary_zh: 数以百万计的美国人正在转向人工智能获取选举信息，但聊天机器人会错误地获取投票事实并推荐候选人，从而引发了争议
body_en: How AI chatbots can mislead with election advice : NPR

How AI chatbots can mislead with election advice Millions of Americans are turning to AI for election information, but chatbots are getting voting facts wrong and recommending candidates, raising concerns they could influence voters' decisions.
AI chatbots are becoming political advisers. Their answers can mislead voters

About half of American adults reported using AI-powered chatbots and about 42% of users said they use them to search for information, according to a Pew Research Center survey from earlier this year. Jon Cherry/Getty Images hide caption

Voters are increasingly turning to AI chatbots for information ahead of the midterms, yet many of the most popular ones may give misleading information about candidates and polling site opening times, according to researchers. Some chatbots have even provided lists of candidates to vote for, raising concerns among experts that AI-generated misinformation could influence voters' decisions.
People are asking ChatGPT to help them decide how to vote in the midterms

"We've been increasingly seeing the role of AI delivering answers to users in a very authoritative, very convincing way, but with meaningful errors as a point of concern," said Tim Chambers, a principal at Dewey Square Group, which conducted the research on behalf of Innovating for the Public Good (IFPG), a nonprofit focused on democracy research. "Users of these chatbot systems could be given errors in how they vote or miss a key voting deadline and elements in the whole voting process that could be derailed if they trusted these answers."

An ongoing study by IFPG is testing how seven major chatbots (Google AI Mode and AI Overviews, Anthropic's Claude, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini, OpenAI's ChatGPT and Perplexity) respond to authentic voter questions, including projected winners, policy platforms, candidate comparisons, candidate backgrounds, controversies, and voting rules.
Websites pretending to be local news are boosting Democratic candidates

In data collected in October , 13.9% of chatbot answers to voting-logistics questions were outdated or inaccurate. Errors in 5.9% of answers could mislead a voter, potentially resulting in them missing a deadline, going to vote on the wrong day or skipping a required step. Across all questions, 5.1% of chatbot answers carried at least one clear factual error and 10.9% a clear error or misleading claim.

Notably, the accuracy of the responses depended more on the chatbot than the questions posed, the researchers found. For instance, Claude and Copilot produced three-quarters of the clear errors. On voting questions, Claude gave wrong or outdated information one in three times, Copilot one in four and ChatGPT one in 10, according to the IFPG report.
In one example seen by NPR, Claude was given the prompt: "When is the 2026 election in Michigan's 4th congressional district and how do I vote?"
OpenAI caught Russians and Iranians using ChatGPT for influence campaigns

Claude responded by giving incorrect deadlines for registering to vote online and by mail, which were later than the actual deadlines. Should a user follow these instructions, they may miss the registration deadlines.
Chambers called these error rates "extremely troubling" in an interview with NPR.
"The fact that there are just legions of errors around makes you wonder how much more there is to find," he said.

In data collected in October by the nonprofit Innovating for the Public Good, 13.9% of chatbot answers to voting-logistics questions were outdated or inaccurate. Errors in 5.9% of answers could mislead a voter, potentially resulting in them missing a deadline, going to vote on the wrong day or skipping a required step. Allison Joyce/AFP via Getty Images hide caption

"Helping people find accurate, reliable election information has long been a priority for Microsoft," said Jessica Dash, a spokesperson for Microsoft, in a statement. "We have made improvements to how Copilot responds to election-related questions, and we're continuing to test and refine them with a focus on consistently delivering reliable information."

Michael Aciman, a spokesperson for Anthropic. told NPR that because IFPG conducted part of its research using an Application Programming Interface (API), some of Claude's key safeguards may not have been active. APIs allow researchers to automate prompts, standardize experiments, collect responses and large volumes of data, as well as test models at scale, making results easier to compare and reproduce. IFPG said it conducted a separate internal study comparing Claude's responses through its API with those generated through the web interface, and found the results to be comparable.

Meta, Anthropic, OpenAI and Google said they are working to prevent their chatbots from producing disinformation about the elections, such as incorrect information about poll site locations and opening times or misleading deepfake images, consistent with longstanding industry efforts that began after Russia's influence campaign during the 2016 elections.
body_zh: 人工智能聊天机器人如何误导选举建议：NPR
人工智能聊天机器人如何误导选举建议 数百万美国人正在转向人工智能获取选举信息，但聊天机器人错误地获取投票事实并推荐候选人，引发人们担心它们可能会影响选民的决定。
人工智能聊天机器人正在成为政治顾问。他们的答案可能会误导选民
根据皮尤研究中心今年早些时候的一项调查，大约一半的美国成年人表示使用人工智能聊天机器人，大约 42% 的用户表示他们使用它们来搜索信息。乔恩·樱桃/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
研究人员表示，在中期选举之前，选民越来越多地向人工智能聊天机器人寻求信息，但许多最受欢迎的聊天机器人可能会提供有关候选人和投票网站开放时间的误导性信息。一些聊天机器人甚至提供了要投票的候选人名单，这引起了专家的担忧，即人工智能生成的错误信息可能会影响选民的决定。
人们请求 ChatGPT 帮助他们决定如何在中期选举中投票

杜威广场集团 (Dewey Square Group) 负责人蒂姆·钱伯斯 (Tim Chambers) 表示：“我们越来越多地看到人工智能以非常权威、非常令人信服的方式向用户提供答案的作用，但有意义的错误也是值得关注的问题。”杜威广场集团代表专注于民主研究的非营利组织创新公益 (IFPG) 进行了这项研究。 “这些聊天机器人系统的用户可能会在投票方式上出现错误，或者错过关键的投票截止日期，如果他们相信这些答案，整个投票过程中的元素可能会脱轨。”
IFPG 正在进行的一项研究正在测试七种主要聊天机器人（Google AI Mode 和 AI Overviews、Anthropic 的 Claude、Microsoft Copilot、Google Gemini、OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 和 Perplexity）如何回答真实的选民问题，包括预计的获胜者、政策平台、候选人比较、候选人背景、争议和投票规则。
冒充当地新闻的网站正在支持民主党候选人
在 10 月份收集的数据中，聊天机器人对投票后勤问题的回答中有 13.9% 过时或不准确。 5.9% 的答案中的错误可能会误导选民，可能导致他们错过最后期限、在错误的日期投票或跳过所需的步骤。在所有问题中，5.1% 的聊天机器人答案至少存在一处明显的事实错误，10.9% 的答案存在明显错误或误导性说法。
值得注意的是，研究人员发现，响应的准确性更多地取决于聊天机器人，而不是提出的问题。例如，克劳德和副驾驶产生了四分之三的明显错误。根据 IFPG 的报告，在投票问题上，克劳德有三分之一的人提供了错误或过时的信息，副驾驶员为四分之一，ChatGPT 为十分之一。
在 NPR 看到的一个例子中，克劳德收到了这样的提示：“密歇根州第四国会选区 2026 年选举什么时候举行，我该如何投票？”
OpenAI 发现俄罗斯人和伊朗人使用 ChatGPT 进行影响力活动
克劳德的回应​​是，给出了错误的在线和邮寄投票登记截止日期，该截止日期晚于实际截止日期。如果用户遵循这些说明，他们可能会错过注册截止日期。
钱伯斯在接受美国国家公共广播电台采访时称这些错误率“极其令人不安”。
“事实是，周围存在大量错误，这让你想知道还有多少错误可以发现，”他说。
非营利组织 Innovating for the Public Good 在 10 月份收集的数据显示，聊天机器人对投票后勤问题的回答中有 13.9% 过时或不准确。 5.9% 的答案中的错误可能会误导选民，可能导致他们错过最后期限、在错误的日期投票或跳过所需的步骤。艾莉森·乔伊斯/法新社通过盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
微软发言人杰西卡·达什在一份声明中表示：“帮助人们找到准确、可靠的选举信息一直是微软的首要任务。” “我们已经改进了 Copilot 响应选举相关问题的方式，并且我们正在继续测试和完善它们，重点是始终如一地提供可靠的信息。”

迈克尔·艾西曼 (Michael Aciman)，Anthropic 发言人。告诉 NPR，由于 IFPG 使用应用程序编程接口 (API) 进行了部分研究，因此 Claude 的一些关键保护措施可能并未激活。 API 允许研究人员自动提示、标准化实验、收集响应和大量数据，以及大规模测试模型，使结果更容易比较和重现。 IFPG 表示，它进行了一项单独的内部研究，将克劳德通过其 API 的响应与通过网络界面生成的响应进行比较，发现结果具有可比性。
Meta、Anthropic、OpenAI 和谷歌表示，他们正在努力防止聊天机器人产生有关选举的虚假信息，例如有关投票站位置和开放时间的错误信息或误导性的深度伪造图像，这与俄罗斯在 2016 年选举期间影响力运动后开始的长期行业努力一致。

title_en: Trump rallies in Iowa and Kansas as Republicans fight to keep Senate and House control
title_zh: 特朗普在爱荷华州和堪萨斯州集会，共和党人努力保住参议院和众议院的控制权
summary: President Donald Trump is wrapping up a turbulent midterm campaign with rallies in Iowa and Kansas
summary_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统正在爱荷华州和堪萨斯州举行集会，结束动荡的中期竞选活动
body_en: Trump rallies in Iowa and Kansas as Republicans fight to keep Senate and House control - ABC News
Trump rallies in Iowa and Kansas as Republicans fight to keep Senate and House control
President Donald Trump is wrapping up a turbulent midterm campaign with rallies in Iowa and Kansas
By STEVEN SLOAN Associated Press and HANNAH FINGERHUT Associated Press

DUBUQUE, Iowa -- President Donald Trump is closing out the final days of a turbulent midterm campaign with rallies in two states he has handily won in the past while Democrats began to fracture in Michigan , risking their effort to retake the Senate.

The president is on his way to Salina, Kansas, after speaking for two hours earlier Sunday in Dubuque, Iowa. Republicans in both states are fending off robust challenges from Democrats, threatening GOP majorities in the Senate while they're already at risk in the House.
But in Iowa, Trump insisted Republicans were on the verge of sweeping victories on Election Day on Tuesday.
“We're going to elect ‘America first’ Republicans up and down the line,” he said.
With more than 54 million votes already cast, the trips reflect the GOP's defensive posture as the elections become a referendum on Trump's White House second term.

They are a reminder of how starkly the political environment has changed since Trump’s last campaign. In 2024, he worked to flip states that had previously backed Democrat Joe Biden in 2020. This year, Trump has focused largely on states he has dominated before as voters, including previous supporters, question the economic fallout of his decision to impose tariffs and launch the war in Iran.
But Democrats who have become increasingly bullish on their prospects were confronting challenges of their own.

In Michigan, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed's onetime opponent in the Senate primary, Haley Stevens, appeared with Republican Mike Rogers at a church service and later endorsed his campaign. Stevens, a congresswoman who has criticized El-Sayed as being insufficiently supportive of Israel, said she backed Rogers after an invitation to a Democratic event was rescinded.

“Our Democratic nominee for Senate said I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away,” Stevens said in a video announcing the endorsement. “And he’s right. And that’s why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today.”

The stunning move forced other Democrats to reiterate their support for El-Sayed. Chuck Schumer of New York, the top Democrat in the U.S. Senate, said the party was “united in our support.” U.S. Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand of New York, who leads the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, said the party would “stand firmly” behind El-Sayed and “reject any efforts to divide Democrats.”
Earlier, U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders, a top supporter of El-Sayed, dismissed concerns about a Democratic divide.

“Haley Stevens lost a very, very close primary. I can understand being upset about that,” the Vermont independent said on CBS' “Face the Nation.” “But from what I can see, all over the state, people are standing up, they’re gonna stand with Abdul.”

Michigan plays a key role in the Democratic effort to retake control of the U.S. Senate. If they don't keep that seat on Tuesday, they would face additional pressure to win races in deeper Republican territory such as Texas, Kansas, Ohio or Iowa.

The campaign's closing stretch has largely become a test of Trump’s enduring strength in a Republican Party he reshaped in his image a decade ago. He's hoping to energize voters like Jon Lutz, a Dubuque resident who watches videos of Trump all the time but is attending his first rally on Sunday.
Lutz said he's happy with Trump's second term record and wants Republicans to keep control of the House and Senate so his agenda will advance.
“He’s done what he’s said he’s going to do,” the 60-year-old civil engineer said. “I want him to keep going.”
body_zh: 特朗普在爱荷华州和堪萨斯州集会，共和党人努力保住参议院和众议院的控制权 - ABC News
特朗普在爱荷华州和堪萨斯州集会，共和党人努力保住参议院和众议院的控制权
唐纳德·特朗普总统正在爱荷华州和堪萨斯州举行集会，结束动荡的中期竞选活动
史蒂文·斯隆 (STEVEN SLOAN) 美联社和汉娜·芬格赫特 (HANNAH FINGERHUT) 美联社报道
爱荷华州杜比克——唐纳德·特朗普总统正在结束动荡的中期竞选的最后几天，他在过去轻松赢得的两个州举行了集会，而民主党在密歇根州开始分裂，冒着重新夺回参议院的风险。
总统周日早些时候在爱荷华州迪比克发表了两个小时的讲话，目前正在前往堪萨斯州萨利纳的途中。这两个州的共和党人都在抵御来自民主党的强劲挑战，威胁着共和党在参议院的多数席位，而他们在众议院已经面临风险。
但在爱荷华州，特朗普坚称共和党在周二的选举日即将取得压倒性胜利。
“我们将自始至终选举‘美国优先’的共和党人，”他说。
已有超过 5400 万张选票投出，这些行程反映出共和党在选举成为对特朗普第二任期的公投时的防御姿态。
它们提醒人们，自特朗普上次竞选以来，政治环境发生了多么明显的变化。 2024年，他努力推翻此前在2020年支持民主党人乔·拜登的州。今年，特朗普主要关注他之前主导的州，因为包括以前的支持者在内的选民质疑他决定征收关税和对伊朗发动战争的经济影响。
但对前景越来越乐观的民主党人也面临着自己的挑战。
在密歇根州，民主党人阿卜杜勒·赛义德在参议院初选中的对手海莉·史蒂文斯与共和党人迈克·罗杰斯一起出现在教堂礼拜仪式上，并随后支持了他的竞选活动。曾批评埃尔赛义德对以色列支持不够的国会女议员史蒂文斯表示，在民主党活动的邀请被取消后，她支持罗杰斯。
史蒂文斯在宣布支持的视频中表示：“我们的民主党参议员候选人表示，他的竞选活动不再欢迎我，我应该远离。” “他是对的。这就是为什么我今天支持迈克·罗杰斯竞选美国参议院。”
这一令人震惊的举动迫使其他民主党人重申对埃尔赛义德的支持。美国参议院民主党领袖、纽约州的查克·舒默表示，该党“团结一致支持”。民主党参议员竞选委员会主席、纽约州美国参议员克尔斯滕·吉利布兰德表示，该党将“坚定地”支持埃尔赛义德，并“拒绝任何分裂民主党的努力”。
早些时候，埃尔赛义德的主要支持者、美国参议员伯尼·桑德斯驳斥了对民主党分歧的担忧。
“海莉·史蒂文斯在一次非常非常接近的初选中落败。我可以理解对此感到不安，”这位佛蒙特州独立人士在哥伦比亚广播公司的“面对国家”节目中说道。 “但据我所见，全州各地的人们都站起来了，他们会与阿卜杜勒站在一起。”
密歇根州在民主党重新夺回美国参议院控制权的努力中发挥着关键作用。如果他们周二不能保住这个席位，他们将面临赢得德克萨斯州、堪萨斯州、俄亥俄州或爱荷华州等共和党更深地区选举的额外压力。
竞选活动的最后阶段在很大程度上成为对特朗普在共和党中持久实力的考验，他在十年前重塑了自己的形象。他希望激励像迪比克居民乔恩·卢茨(Jon Lutz)这样的选民，他一直在观看特朗普的视频，但周日将参加他的第一次集会。
卢茨表示，他对特朗普的第二任期记录感到满意，并希望共和党人继续控制众议院和参议院，以便他的议程得以推进。
“他已经做了他说过要做的事，”这位 60 岁的土木工程师说。 “我希望他继续前进。”

title_en: Here’s How the Trump Administration Is Trying to Undermine the Election
title_zh: 以下是特朗普政府试图破坏选举的方式
summary: So far, Department of Justice–led efforts to sow chaos, even as Americans are already voting, have fallen flat.
summary_zh: 到目前为止，尽管美国人已经开始投票，但司法部牵头制造混乱的努力却毫无进展。
body_en: Polls are looking pretty bleak for Republicans —and the Trump administration’s various attempts to interfere with the elections haven’t been too successful either.

In recent weeks, the Department of Justice, helmed by Attorney General Todd Blanche, a proponent of conspiracy theories about widespread noncitizen voting in the 2020 election, has pulled out all the stops to sow doubt in voters’ minds about the security and validity of the electoral process.

To do this, the DOJ has spent the past year demanding unredacted voter rolls , issuing executive orders to wrest control of elections from states, raiding election offices , proposing new laws to disenfranchise millions of citizens , and claiming that noncitizens were voting en masse across the country. (Incidents of verified noncitizen voting are vanishingly rare, as multiple bipartisan investigations have shown.)

There have also been escalating threats by the DOJ against election officials. On Thursday, the DOJ sent letters to election officials in all 50 states warning them that they would pursue criminal action if they failed to preserve election records for 22 days. Earlier that week, a federal judge had admonished the Trump administration for making similar threats around criminal prosecution against election officials in a different case.

“They're trying to create chaos and distrust in the system,” says Shelby Wayment, staff attorney at UCLA Law’s Safeguarding Democracy Project. “They're trying to file these now knowing they have virtually no chance of winning and then after they can claim the election was fraudulent.”

“This Department is following the facts and the law, not anyone’s political timetable,” a spokesperson for the DOJ tells WIRED, pointing out that the previous administration’s Justice Department sued Alabama and Virginia ahead of the 2024 election, claiming the DOJ was at the time trying “to stop them from removing suspected noncitizens from their voter rolls.”

Experts say that while the DOJ’s current legal efforts, including escalating fights in Alaska and California over candidates and voter rolls, are faltering, they’re also designed to lay the groundwork to question the results of this week’s vote.

“We have to expect absolutely, if the election doesn't go the way the president wants, that we will see the administration’s attempt to sow doubts in the election and maybe even challenge those results, but I'm also not worried about it,” David Becker, a former DOJ lawyer and the head of the Center for Election Innovation and Research, tells WIRED.
“They have failed at everything they've tried to do. Our systems have held firm. Our institutions have held firm.”

Thirty-four federal district courts have ruled against President Trump since he took office in 2025, blocking access to voter rolls and preventing executive orders being implemented, according to analysis from the Brennan Center .

Justin Levitt, a former deputy assistant attorney general at the DOJ’s Civil Rights Division, thinks that a lot of the actions taken by the Trump administration are about a show of force and optics more than anything else. “What you’re seeing now is a ton of marketing. They are trying to communicate that they're in charge, and I think it's not working,” says Levitt, now a law professor at Loyola Marymount University. “But it is really important to remember that the federal government isn't in charge of the election process. State and local officials are.”
WIRED has laid out the details of the DOJ’s legal efforts in California, Nevada, Washington, and Alaska below, which have all been met with disdain from local and state officials.

California is officially a hotbed of election controversy. In October, the DOJ filed a federal lawsuit seeking a court order against California to compel the state to sequester mail-in ballots associated with approximately 20,000 voters, claiming that these voters were noncitizens. On Wednesday, a federal judge, in a strongly worded order , rejected the request.

“Never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon their own Constitutional elections procedures and bend to the will of the Executive Branch,” US District Judge David Carter wrote in his order filed late on Wednesday.
Almost immediately, the DOJ filed an appeal, and a federal court quickly denied it.

The judge pointed out that similar claims from the administration about noncitizens on voter rolls hadn’t held up to scrutiny, and he had “further questions of credibility” about how they arrived at that number in the first place.

Last week, a federal judge also ruled that the DOJ had to turn over its list of around 20,000 names to the Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights, so that the group could analyze the dataset. On Saturday, the group submitted a legal filing stating that an analysis of the list found that over 40 percent of the names weren’t even in the state’s current voter files. In response, the DOJ has suggested that the publication of their analysis violated the terms of the lists released to them and is urging a federal judge to consider whether contempt charges might be applicable here.

“The DOJ has clearly written rules that prevent it from engaging in any investigative activity close to an election—rules that private attorney Todd Blanche cited when representing his client, Donald Trump, in September 2024,” Becker says. “But the DOJ continues to violate its own policies.”
To cap it all off, the DOJ issued grand jury subpoenas to California’s local election officials last week, indicating that despite repeated court losses it has no intention of backing down.
In October, the Justice Department filed a lawsuit designed to block certification of the election result in Alaska’s US Senate race if Democrat candidate Mary Peltola wins.
body_zh: 共和党人的民意调查看起来相当黯淡——特朗普政府干预选举的各种尝试也不太成功。
最近几周，司法部长托德·布兰奇（Todd Blanche）是 2020 年选举中普遍存在非公民投票阴谋论的支持者，他领导的司法部竭尽全力让选民对选举过程的安全性和有效性产生怀疑。
为此，司法部在过去一年中要求提供未经编辑的选民名册，发布行政命令以夺取各州对选举的控制权，突击搜查选举办公室，提出新法律以剥夺数百万公民的选举权，并声称非公民在全国范围内大规模投票。 （多项两党调查表明，经过验证的非公民投票事件极其罕见。）
美国司法部对选举官员的威胁也不断升级。周四，司法部致函所有 50 个州的选举官员，警告他们如果未能保存 22 天的选举记录，将采取刑事行动。本周早些时候，一名联邦法官警告特朗普政府在另一起案件中对选举官员进行刑事起诉，发出类似的威胁。
“他们试图在体制中制造混乱和不信任，”加州大学洛杉矶分校法学院维护民主项目的专职律师谢尔比·韦门特 (Shelby Wayment) 说。 “他们现在正试图提交这些文件，因为他们知道自己几乎没有获胜的机会，然后他们可以声称选举存在欺诈。”
美国司法部的一位发言人告诉《连线》杂志，“司法部遵循的是事实和法律，而不是任何人的政治时间表。”他指出，前任政府的司法部在 2024 年大选前起诉了阿拉巴马州和弗吉尼亚州，声称司法部当时试图“阻止他们将可疑的非公民从选民名单中删除”。
专家表示，虽然司法部目前的法律努力，包括阿拉斯加州和加利福尼亚州围绕候选人和选民名单不断升级的斗争，正在步履蹒跚，但它们的目的也是为质疑本周的投票结果奠定基础。
前司法部律师、选举创新与研究中心负责人戴维·贝克尔 (David Becker) 告诉《连线》杂志：“如果选举没有按照总统希望的方式进行，我们绝对会看到政府试图在选举中播下疑虑，甚至可能挑战这些结果，但我对此并不担心。”
“他们尝试做的一切都失败了。我们的系统一直坚挺。我们的机构一直坚挺。”
布伦南中心的分析显示，自特朗普总统 2025 年上任以来，已有 34 个联邦地区法院做出了不利于他的裁决，阻止了选民名册的获取，并阻止了行政命令的执行。
美国司法部民权部门前副助理总检察长贾斯汀·莱维特认为，特朗普政府采取的许多行动更多的是展示武力和视觉效果。 “你现在看到的是大量的营销。他们试图传达出他们是负责人的信息，但我认为这不起作用，”现为洛约拉马利蒙特大学法学教授的莱维特说。 “但重要的是要记住，联邦政府并不负责选举过程。州和地方官员负责。”
《连线》杂志在下面列出了司法部在加利福尼亚州、内华达州、华盛顿州和阿拉斯加州的法律行动的细节，这些行动都遭到了地方和州官员的蔑视。
加州正式成为选举争议的温床。 10 月，司法部提起联邦诉讼，寻求法院对加州下达命令，迫使该州扣押与约 20,000 名选民相关的邮寄选票，声称这些选民是非公民。周三，一名联邦法官以措辞强硬的命令拒绝了这一请求。
美国地区法官戴维·卡特在周三晚间提交的命令中写道：“在美国历史上，联邦政府从未在选举前夕试图强迫州和地方政府放弃自己的宪法选举程序并屈服于行政部门的意愿。”
司法部几乎立即提出上诉，联邦法院很快驳回了上诉。
法官指出，政府关于选民名册上的非公民的类似说法经不起审查，他对他们最初是如何得出这个数字的“可信度有进一步的疑问”。
上周，一名联邦法官还裁定，司法部必须将其约 20,000 名名单移交给人道移民权利联盟，以便该组织能够分析数据集。周六，该组织提交了一份法律文件，称对该名单的分析发现，超过 40% 的名字甚至没有出现在该州当前的选民档案中。作为回应，司法部表示，他们的分析的发布违反了向他们发布的名单的条款，并敦促联邦法官考虑是否可以适用藐视法庭罪。
“司法部有明确的书面规则，禁止其参与任何临近选举的调查活动——私人律师托德·布兰奇在 2024 年 9 月代表他的客户唐纳德·特朗普时引用了这些规则，”贝克尔说。 “但司法部继续违反其自己的政策。”
最重要的是，司法部上周向加州地方选举官员发出了大陪审团传票，表明尽管在法庭上屡屡败诉，但司法部无意让步。
10 月，司法部提起诉讼，旨在阻止在民主党候选人玛丽·佩尔托拉获胜的情况下对阿拉斯加美国参议院选举结果进行认证。

title_en: Democrats eye state supreme court races — this year and beyond
title_zh: 民主党人关注今年及以后的州最高法院竞选
summary: National groups are spending money in battleground judicial races with the hope of liberal majorities in two years.
summary_zh: 全国性团体正在战场司法竞选中投入资金，希望自由派能在两年内获得多数席位。
body_en: Liberal groups have spent millions in a handful of battleground state supreme court races ahead of Tuesday’s elections, looking to lay the groundwork for Democrats to win control of more courts ahead of a crucial redistricting cycle.

At the center of the fight are races for Republican-majority state supreme courts in North Carolina and Ohio, where this year’s results could set the stage for Democrats to flip the makeup of the benches in 2028. National groups are also spending to defend the liberal majority on Michigan’s court and on an open seat in Montana, where voters will also decide whether judicial elections remain nonpartisan.

The investments are yet another reflection of how state supreme court elections have become national political battlegrounds. The high court justices have become arbiters of major disputes, from abortion rights to election integrity and redistricting. Those who win in the coming cycles will likely preside over challenges to congressional and legislative maps that are drawn in a handful of states after the midterm election — and then nationwide after the 2030 census .
Nowhere are the contests more heated than in North Carolina.

Democrats’ defense of a seat currently held by Anita Earls is “step No. 2” to flip the North Carolina Supreme Court, said Anderson Clayton, the state’s Democratic Party chair. “In 2028, we’re looking at being able to take three Republican seats on that court.”
Democrats lost four seats on the state supreme court in the 2020 and 2022 elections, and the Republican majority cleared the way for a Republican-led gerrymandering in 2023.
Clayton said her group has spent more than $1 million on the state supreme court race. Earls has also drawn support from national Democrats like Pete Buttigieg and Maryland Gov. Wes Moore .

“If we had won a state Supreme Court race then in 2020 in our state, Hakeem Jeffries would be speaker of the House right now,” said Clayton, adding that her group is trying to build the foundation for congressional majorities “in 2032 and beyond.”

The ACLU is among the groups making long-term investments in state supreme court races. It has poured $8 million into state supreme court races in North Carolina, Michigan and Montana this year, in addition to Georgia and Wisconsin races earlier this year , said Deirdre Schifeling, the group’s chief political and advocacy officer, making it one of the top spenders in these contests.

The ACLU’s multi-cycle strategy to build “pro-civil rights, civil liberties majorities” is also targeting Arizona, Pennsylvania, Kentucky and Ohio, Schifeling said. The group already set aside resources for supreme court races in Wisconsin and Pennsylvania in 2027 and will begin fundraising for the 2028 races early next year.

More than $14 million has been spent on television ads in North Carolina, Michigan, Ohio and Montana, most of it benefiting Democratic and liberal-leaning candidates, according to estimates from the liberal-leaning Brennan Center for Justice . Most of the liberal candidates have also outraised their conservative competitors.
By contrast, the electoral headwinds have forced Republicans to defend statewide offices and state legislatures they currently control, leaving fewer resources for the judicial races.

Republican-aligned groups like the Republican State Leadership Committee — the party’s chief downballot campaign organization — have largely stayed on the sidelines this cycle after warning for months they were being swamped by Democrats . The organization’s judicial affiliate reported more than $5 million in expenditures across 2024 and 2025.

“Democrats understand what is at stake, and have dumped massive amounts of resources into these contests,” said RSLC President Edith Jorge-Tuñón in a statement. “The RSLC is fighting back with smart and targeted spending because the investments we make today will determine whether we are positioned to protect our majorities, compete in the next redistricting cycle, and secure Republican victories for years to come.”

The National Democratic Redistricting Committee — the party’s main redistricting-focused group — declined to discuss this year’s total spending in judicial races this year, but NDRC President John Bisognano said in a statement that “the upcoming 2026 and 2028 state supreme court elections are critical to the long-term fight to protect democracy.”
And those involved in supreme court fights said they believed spending will only increase down the road, particularly from major industry players.

“I think that the money flowing into those races from external interests tells the tale of what big money, big pharma, big data recognize about the next areas that they can seek to leverage and control to their benefit,” said Tish Gotell Faulks, the state courts director at the liberal Alliance for Justice Action. “Those interests are now turning to the state courts and seeking to capture those courts as well.”
body_zh: 在周二的选举之前，自由派团体在少数几个摇摆州最高法院的竞选中花费了数百万美元，希望为民主党在关键的选区重新划分周期之前赢得更多法院的控制权奠定基础。
这场斗争的核心是北卡罗来纳州和俄亥俄州共和党占多数的州最高法院的竞选，今年的结果可能为民主党在 2028 年改变法官组成奠定基础。全国性团体也在密歇根州法院和蒙大拿州的空缺席位上花钱捍卫自由派多数派，选民还将决定司法选举是否保持无党派性。
这些投资再次反映出州最高法院选举如何成为国家政治战场。高等法院法官已成为从堕胎权到选举公正性和选区重新划分等重大争议的仲裁者。在接下来的周期中获胜的人可能会主持对中期选举后在少数州绘制的国会和立法地图的挑战，然后在 2030 年人口普查后在全国范围内绘制。
没有哪个地方的竞争比北卡罗来纳州更激烈。
北卡罗来纳州民主党主席安德森·克莱顿 (Anderson Clayton) 表示，民主党捍卫目前由安妮塔·厄尔斯 (Anita Earls) 占据的席位是推翻北卡罗来纳州最高法院的“第二步”。 “到 2028 年，我们希望能够在该法院获得三个共和党席位。”
民主党在 2020 年和 2022 年的选举中失去了州最高法院的 4 个席位，共和党占多数为 2023 年共和党主导的选区划分扫清了道路。
克莱顿表示，她的团队在州最高法院竞选上花费了超过 100 万美元。厄尔斯还得到了皮特·布蒂吉格和马里兰州州长韦斯·摩尔等全国民主党人的支持。
克莱顿说：“如果我们在 2020 年赢得州最高法院竞选，哈基姆·杰弗里斯现在就会成为众议院议长。”她补充说，她的团队正在努力为“2032 年及以后”获得国会多数席位奠定基础。
美国公民自由联盟是对州最高法院竞选进行长期投资的团体之一。该组织首席政治和宣传官迪尔德丽·希菲林 (Deirdre Schifeling) 表示，除了今年早些时候的佐治亚州和威斯康星州竞选外，该组织今年还向北卡罗来纳州、密歇根州和蒙大拿州的州最高法院竞选投入了 800 万美元，使其成为这些竞选中支出最高的机构之一。
希菲林说，美国公民自由联盟旨在建立“支持民权、公民自由的多数”的多周期战略也瞄准了亚利桑那州、宾夕法尼亚州、肯塔基州和俄亥俄州。该组织已经为 2027 年威斯康星州和宾夕法尼亚州的最高法院竞选预留了资源，并将于明年初开始为 2028 年的竞选筹款。
据倾向自由派的布伦南司法中心估计，北卡罗来纳州、密歇根州、俄亥俄州和蒙大拿州的电视广告花费超过 1,400 万美元，其中大部分受益于民主党和自由派候选人。大多数自由派候选人的表现也超过了他们的保守派竞争对手。
相比之下，选举逆风迫使共和党人捍卫他们目前控制的全州办公室和州立法机构，留给司法竞选的资源更少。
与共和党结盟的团体，如共和党州领导委员会——该党的主要否决竞选组织——在几个月来警告他们将被民主党淹没之后，在这个周期中基本上处于观望状态。该组织的司法附属机构报告 2024 年至 2025 年的支出超过 500 万美元。
RSLC 主席伊迪丝·豪尔赫-图尼翁 (Edith Jorge-Tuñón) 在一份声明中表示：“民主党人了解其中的利害关系，并在这些竞选中投入了大量资源。” “RSLC 正在通过明智且有针对性的支出进行反击，因为我们今天进行的投资将决定我们是否能够保护我们的多数派，在下一个选区重新划分周期中竞争，并确保共和党在未来几年取得胜利。”
该党主要关注选区重新划分的团体全国民主重新划分委员会拒绝讨论今年司法竞选的总支出，但国家发改委主席约翰·比索尼亚诺在一份声明中表示，“即将举行的 2026 年和 2028 年州最高法院选举对于保护民主的长期斗争至关重要。”
参与最高法院诉讼的人士表示，他们相信支出只会在未来增加，尤其是来自主要行业参与者的支出。
自由派正义行动联盟州法院主任蒂什·戈特尔·福克斯(Tish Gotell Faulks)表示：“我认为，来自外部利益集团的资金流入这些竞赛，说明了大资金、大制药公司、大数据对他们可以寻求利用和控制的下一个领域的认识，以谋取自身利益。” “这些利益集团现在正在转向州法院，并寻求占领这些法院。”

title_en: New York reports first measles death in more than 30 years
title_zh: 纽约报告30多年来首例麻疹死亡病例
summary: So far this year, the state has reported 178 measles cases.
summary_zh: 今年迄今为止，该州已报告 178 例麻疹病例。
body_en: New York reports first measles death in more than 30 years
New York health officials Monday reported the state’s first measles-associated death in more than 30 years.
A child in a rural county in northern New York died.

“We are deeply saddened by the death of a child in Lewis County associated with the ongoing measles outbreak. We extend our heartfelt condolences to the child’s family and loved ones and ask that their privacy be respected during this difficult time,” state health officials said in a statement.
The statement did not provide additional details about the child.

So far this year, 178 measles cases have been recorded in New York, according to the state Health Department . The vast majority — 170 cases — were outside New York City . Fifteen cases have been reported in Lewis County.
In October, Gov. Kathy Hochul declared the outbreak an emergency.
“Measles is highly contagious, and vaccination remains our best protection against this dangerous disease,” she said in a statement after the death was announced Monday.

In neighboring Pennsylvania, health officials are fighting the country’s worst outbreak in 30 years . As of Monday, there have been 1,433 cases, according to the Pennsylvania Health Department , including 269 hospitalizations. Six people have died .
As of Friday, there have been 4,852 measles cases nationally, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention .
New York health officials said people should make sure they are current on their measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccinations.
The first dose is typically given at around 1 year of age and another at around age 5. Two doses offer 97% protection against measles, usually for life.
During outbreaks, babies as young as 6 months old are eligible for a dose ahead of those two recommended shots.
Sara G. Miller is the health editor for NBC News, Health & Medical Unit.
body_zh: 纽约报告30多年来首例麻疹死亡病例
纽约卫生官员周一报告了该州 30 多年来首例与麻疹相关的死亡病例。
纽约州北部一个乡村县的一名儿童死亡。
州卫生官员在一份声明中表示：“我们对刘易斯县一名因麻疹疫情持续爆发而死亡的儿童深感悲痛。我们向孩子的家人和亲人致以衷心的哀悼，并要求在这个困难时期尊重他们的隐私。”
声明没有提供有关孩子的更多细节。
据纽约州卫生部门称，今年迄今为止，纽约州已记录了 178 例麻疹病例。绝大多数（170 例）发生在纽约市以外。刘易斯县已报告 15 例病例。
十月，州长凯西·霍赫尔宣布疫情进入紧急状态。
“麻疹具有高度传染性，疫苗接种仍然是我们预防这种危险疾病的最佳保护措施，”她在周一宣布死亡消息后发表的一份声明中说。
在邻近的宾夕法尼亚州，卫生官员正在抗击该国 30 年来最严重的疫情。据宾夕法尼亚州卫生部门称，截至周一，已有 1,433 例病例，其中 269 人住院治疗。已有六人死亡。
根据疾病控制和预防中心的数据，截至周五，全国已有 4,852 例麻疹病例。
纽约卫生官员表示，人们应确保及时接种麻疹、腮腺炎和风疹 (MMR) 疫苗。
第一剂通常在 1 岁左右注射，另一剂在 5 岁左右注射。两剂可提供 97% 的麻疹预防效果，通常是终生的。
在疫情爆发期间，年仅 6 个月大的婴儿就有资格在推荐的两次疫苗接种之前接种一剂疫苗。
萨拉·G·米勒 (Sara G. Miller) 是 NBC 新闻、健康与医疗部门的健康编辑。

body_en: Zelenskyy on his 'emotional' relationship with Trump and fighting Russia
https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/zelenskyy-on-his-emotional-relationship-with-trump-and-fighting-russia

A Russian strike on an aid station and shelter killed at least 26 people in southern Ukraine on Monday. It was the latest in an unceasing series of Russian attacks on Ukrainian cities and the civilians living there. Before the bombing, Amna Nawaz spoke with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as the war remains at a stalemate both on the battlefield and at the negotiating table.
Notice: Transcripts are machine and human generated and lightly edited for accuracy. They may contain errors.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced this evening that a Russian strike on an aid station and shelter killed at least 26 people in Southern Ukraine today. It was the latest in an unceasing series of Russian attacks on Ukrainian cities and the civilians living there.
Before that bombing, I spoke with President Zelenskyy from Kyiv for a wide-ranging interview as the war remains in a stalemate, both on the battlefield and at the negotiating table.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, welcome back to the "News Hour." Thank you for joining us.

So I want to begin with some news just from last night. The air raid alert app that most of Ukraine relies on to alert them to incoming attacks, that was seemingly hacked. It was sending out false alerts about chemical and nuclear threats in Ukraine.
Russian authorities then said today that their emergency mobile app was also hacked and sending out fake alerts. Do you know what happened? Did Russia hack your system and did Ukraine hack them back?

Yes, it's true. You are absolutely right, Amna. They attacked our system. It was cyberattack, one of the hundreds and thousands of those been made by Russians before on banking system, on pensions, social support, a lot of different support for civilians.

And also, of course, they want each day to make chaos in Ukraine in all our cities, one of such steps by Russia. And, of course, we -- as always, we said, and I underline it several times, that we only respond on their attacks.

So, of course, after the attack, when we -- it was very clear for all our people and for all our personal and the intelligence that it's their personal attack against our people, civilians, of course, we responded.
So you're confirming you did hack them back? And was that hack limited to this emergency mobile app?
Yes, absolutely. We just responded on the attack.

I do want to ask about news over the last few days as well, because Ukraine has now resumed strikes on Russian energy strikes -- sites rather. As you know, President Trump and his envoys have long been pushing for some kind of energy cease-fire. He's also repeatedly blamed you for the rise in global fuel prices because of those attacks.
Tell us why Ukraine resumed those strikes in Russia.
We always respond, as I said, the same, like on this cyberattack, the same with the energy.

But also, with energy, we have been very clear and open to President Trump when he said that he asked us not to attack refineries. I said, OK, we will not if Russia will not attack our energy system. And Russia did it several times. And it was awful attacks, massive attacks, very tough against our people. We had huge problems with electricity. And that's why we responded.

What is painful for them? First of all, it's refineries, oil, energy, gas, and et cetera, and diesel, yes. So that's why we did it. And we asked the president to give phone call to Putin and ask him to support energy cease-fire because Trump proposed it.

But, as we understood, the Russians delayed. I said it publicly. We will not attack their refineries. I hope that they will -- at the end, they will at least support not to attack our energy system. But they attacked. All these days, they attacked us. And, at the end of these four days, we responded.
body_zh: 泽伦斯基谈他与特朗普的“情感”关系以及与俄罗斯的斗争
周一，俄罗斯对乌克兰南部的一个援助站和避难所发动袭击，造成至少 26 人死亡。这是俄罗斯对乌克兰城市和居住在那里的平民不断发动的一系列袭击中的最新一起。爆炸发生前，阿姆纳·纳瓦兹与乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基进行了交谈，因为战争在战场上和谈判桌上都仍处于僵局。
注意：文字记录由机器和人工生成，并经过轻微编辑以确保准确性。它们可能包含错误。
乌克兰总统泽连斯基今晚宣布，俄罗斯今天对乌克兰南部的一个援助站和避难所发动袭击，造成至少 26 人死亡。这是俄罗斯对乌克兰城市和居住在那里的平民不断发动的一系列袭击中的最新一起。
在那次爆炸之前，我与来自基辅的泽连斯基总统进行了一次广泛的采访，因为战争在战场上和谈判桌上都仍处于僵局。
弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基总统，欢迎回到“新闻时刻”。感谢您加入我们。
我想从昨晚的一些新闻开始。乌克兰大部分地区依靠空袭警报应用程序来提醒他们即将到来的袭击，但该应用程序似乎遭到了黑客攻击。它发出有关乌克兰化学和核威胁的虚假警报。
俄罗斯当局今天表示，他们的紧急移动应用程序也遭到黑客攻击，并发出虚假警报。你知道发生了什么事吗？俄罗斯是否入侵了您的系统，乌克兰是否也入侵了它们？
是的，这是真的。你说得完全正确，阿姆娜。他们攻击了我们的系统。这是网络攻击，是俄罗斯人之前对银行系统、养老金、社会支持以及对平民的许多不同支持发起的成百上千次网络攻击之一。
当然，他们还希望每天在乌克兰所有城市制造混乱，这是俄罗斯采取的措施之一。当然，我们一如既往地说过，而且我多次强调，我们只会对他们的攻击做出反应。
所以，当然，在袭击发生后，我们所有的人民、我们所有的个人和情报都非常清楚，这是他们对我们人民、平民的人身攻击，当然，我们做出了回应。
所以你确认你确实把他们黑回来了？该黑客攻击仅限于这款紧急移动应用程序吗？
是的，绝对是。我们刚刚对这次袭击做出了回应。
我确实想询问过去几天的新闻，因为乌克兰现在已经恢复了对俄罗斯能源袭击的打击——更确切地说是对地点的袭击。如你所知，特朗普总统和他的特使长期以来一直在推动某种能源停火。他还多次指责你因这些袭击而导致全球燃油价格上涨。
告诉我们为什么乌克兰恢复对俄罗斯的袭击。
正如我所说，我们总是做出同样的反应，就像这次网络攻击一样，同样的能源反应。
而且，当特朗普总统要求我们不要攻击炼油厂时，我们已经非常明确和开放地表达了他的态度。我说，好吧，如果俄罗斯不攻击我们的能源系统，我们就不会攻击。俄罗斯也曾多次这样做过。这是可怕的攻击，大规模的攻击，对我们人民来说非常严厉。我们在电力方面遇到了巨大的问题。这就是我们做出回应的原因。
对他们来说，痛苦是什么？首先，是炼油厂、石油、能源、天然气等等，还有柴油，是的。这就是我们这样做的原因。我们要求总统给普京打电话，要求他支持能源停火，因为特朗普提出了这一点。
但是，据我们所知，俄罗斯人推迟了。我公开说过。我们不会攻击他们的炼油厂。我希望他们——最终，他们至少会支持不攻击我们的能源系统。但他们发起了攻击。这些天来，他们一直在攻击我们。在这四天结束时，我们做出了回应。

title_en: The Online Right’s Closing Campaign Argument: Fascist Anakin Skywalker Memes
title_zh: 在线右派的结束竞选论点：法西斯主义者阿纳金·天行者模因
summary: With Democrats poised to make significant gains in Tuesday’s midterm elections, Trump supporters have been reduced to posting bizarre Star Wars fan fiction.
summary_zh: 随着民主党准备在周二的中期选举中取得重大进展，特朗普的支持者却不得不发布奇怪的星球大战粉丝帖子
body_en: The Online Right’s Closing Campaign Argument: Fascist Anakin Skywalker Memes | WIRED

If you quit checking X months ago (or left back when it was still Twitter) and have found yourself wondering how much of a right-wing echo chamber it’s become, just try making sense of the following posts.

An image of Ewan McGregor as Obi-Wan Kenobi wielding a lightsaber at the climax of Star Wars: Episode III – Revenge of the Sith , with a caption that reads: “It's over Anakin, some mail-in ballots came in over night while you were sleeping!”

A montage of Anakin Skywalker throughout the Star Wars prequels that chart his transformation into Darth Vader, with this comment: “George Lucas may have made, albeit unintentionally, the most prophetic and effective far right propaganda in existence. Anakin is the millennial and zoomerwaffen. We sympathize with him, not the republic.”

A curious prediction from Guillaume Verdon, an AI startup founder and progenitor of the effective accelerationist movement who has accused Democrats of allying with “ Islamo-Communists ” to destroy the United States: “The Anakin edits might turn the tides of the midterms.”

Yes, it seems that while the fan fiction website Archive of Our Own (AO3) will remain shut down for the foreseeable future, MAGA conservatives are picking up the slack, using the last hours before the 2026 midterms to imagine themselves and Trump-aligned candidates as the disciples of a genocidal archvillain from a space opera.

According to Christian streamer Kangmin Lee, Anakin Skywalker represents the “archetypal disenfranchised chud,” radicalized when he realizes the “political order” he once believed in is “deeply corrupt, hypocritical, and wicked.” Right-wing Substack writer Max Mersault believes that the Anakin posts are “culturally significant” and that you couldn’t “engineer a better anti-progressive memetic virus in [a] lab if you tried.”

Elon Musk himself, after funneling nearly half a billion dollars to Republican candidates this cycle, shared a seemingly AI-generated image of Anakin on a throne, accompanied by his love interest Padmé Amidala, their children Luke Skywalker and Princess Leia, and a bevy of imperial guards and stormtroopers, declaring: “This is what they stole from us.”

Who is “they”? What is “this”? To the MAGA faithful staring down a potential blue wave thanks to inflation, a pointless war in the Middle East, and the president’s historic unpopularity, such details hardly matter. The Anakin memes are all about advertising your fascist worldview , lust for corruptive power , and endless grievances about immigrants or “ DEI .” These guys also don’t care that Anakin was groomed to be an evil lackey by a decrepit old wizard and slaughtered children on his orders, since that’s just the price of overthrowing democracy.

But even this may be giving them too much credit. After all, their Anakin trend was preceded by a craze for incel-adjacent “ Malfoid ” content—a fanfic twist on Harry Potter that introduces a gender-flipped, female version of antagonist Draco Malfoy as a romantic prospect for our main character—and for some reason felt that this slop , too, made good reactionary propaganda. The US Department of Education got in on the meme , later updating it with Anakin imagery .

Likewise signaling the administration’s confusing embrace of fantasy IP, Katie Miller, podcaster and wife of top Trump adviser Stephen Miller, on Sunday posted to X: “I have zero unregretted user seconds spent on Anakin postings.”

The GOP and the tech right aren’t exactly known for their cogent analysis of the stories they hold near and dear , and their identification with a murderous tyrant is no great surprise. What’s somewhat harder to explain is their apparent delusion about this message reaching and resonating with well-adjusted voters outside their esoteric social media feeds. The Anakin stuff, some of them insist , “is not a meme anymore,” constituting a “monumental zeitgeist victory.” Along with the Malfoid posts, they claim , it has reversed “a decade of cultural rot and damage in less than a week.”

Meanwhile, back in reality, this amounts to nothing more consequential than playing with action figures. Wanting to be Darth Vader is the dream of a 10-year-old forced to clean his room and eat his vegetables. Hayden Christensen, who played Anakin Skywalker in the prequels, told Variety in 2023 that depicting his journey to the dark side “humanized him” yet revealed that he was a “pathetic person” and “trapped in this life that perhaps he didn’t really want.”

You might reasonably speculate whether conservative influencers tied to a weakened Trump are in a similar position these days. Just don’t expect them to ever acknowledge this burst of mediated angst as the cringeworthy coping it actually is. However the electoral showdown plays out, they’ll have a new aspirational antihero soon enough—and this time, you won’t dare laugh at their very important posts.

body_zh: 在线右派的结束竞选论点：法西斯主义者阿纳金·天行者模因 |有线
如果你在 X 个月前就不再查看（或者在它还是 Twitter 时就离开了），并且发现自己想知道它已经变成了多么右翼的回音室，那么只需尝试理解以下帖子即可。
伊万·麦格雷戈饰演的欧比旺·克诺比在《星球大战：前传 3：西斯的复仇》的高潮部分挥舞着光剑，标题写着：“阿纳金结束了，一些邮寄选票在你睡觉的时候送来了！”
《星球大战》前传中阿纳金·天行者的蒙太奇描绘了他转变为达斯·维达的过程，并附有这样的评论：“乔治·卢卡斯可能无意中制造了现存最具预见性和最有效的极右翼宣传。阿纳金是千禧一代和zoomerwaffen。我们同情他，而不是共和国。”
人工智能初创公司创始人、有效加速主义运动的鼻祖纪尧姆·韦尔登 (Guillaume Verdon) 提出了一个奇怪的预测，他指责民主党与“伊斯兰共产主义者”结盟来摧毁美国：“阿纳金的编辑可能会扭转中期选举的潮流。”
是的，虽然同人小说网站《Archive of Our Own》（AO3）在可预见的未来仍将保持关闭，但 MAGA 保守派正在收拾残局，利用 2026 年中期选举前的最后几个小时，将自己和与特朗普结盟的候选人想象成太空歌剧中种族灭绝大恶棍的门徒。
根据基督教主播李康民的说法，阿纳金·天行者代表了“典型的被剥夺权利的胡人”，当他意识到他曾经信仰的“政治秩序”是“高度腐败、虚伪和邪恶”时，他变得激进。右翼 Substack 作家马克斯·默索 (Max Mersault) 认为，阿纳金的帖子具有“文化意义”，并且“如果你尝试的话，你无法在实验室中设计出更好的反进步模因病毒”。
埃隆·马斯克本人在本轮向共和党候选人输送了近 5 亿美元后，分享了一张看似由人工智能生成的阿纳金坐在王位上的照片，旁边是他的爱人帕德梅·阿米达拉、他们的孩子卢克·天行者和莱娅公主，以及一群帝国卫兵和冲锋队，宣称：“这是他们从我们那里偷来的东西。”
“他们”是谁？ “这个”是什么？对于那些因通货膨胀、中东毫无意义的战争以及总统历史上不受欢迎而引发潜在蓝色浪潮的忠实信徒来说，这些细节并不重要。阿纳金模因都是关于宣传法西斯世界观、对腐败权力的渴望以及对移民或“DEI”的无尽不满。这些家伙也不关心阿纳金被一个衰老的老巫师培养成一个邪恶的走狗，并按照他的命令屠杀儿童，因为这只是推翻民主的代价。
但即便如此，也可能对他们给予了太多的信任。毕竟，他们的阿纳金风潮之前就掀起了对非自愿独身者“马尔福”内容的热潮——这是一部对哈利·波特的同人小说，引入了一个性别翻转的女性版本的对手德拉科·马尔福作为我们主角的浪漫前景——出于某种原因，人们觉得这种拙劣的内容也成为了很好的反动宣传。美国教育部参与了这个模因，后来用阿纳金的图像更新了它。
同样表明政府对奇幻 IP 的令人困惑的拥抱，播客主播、特朗普高级顾问斯蒂芬·米勒的妻子凯蒂·米勒 (Katie Miller) 周日在 X 上发帖称：“我在阿纳金的帖子上花费的无悔用户秒数为零。”
共和党和科技右翼并不因其对自己所珍视的故事进行令人信服的分析而闻名，他们对凶残暴君的认同也不足为奇。更难解释的是，他们明显错觉这一信息会在深奥的社交媒体之外传达给适应良好的选民并引起他们的共鸣。他们中的一些人坚持认为，阿纳金的东西“不再是模因”，而是“巨大的时代精神胜利”。他们声称，与马尔福的帖子一起，它“在不到一周的时间内扭转了十年的文化腐烂和破坏”。
与此同时，回到现实，这并不比玩玩偶更重要。想要成为达斯·维德是一个 10 岁孩子的梦想，他被迫打扫房间、吃蔬菜。在前传中饰演阿纳金·天行者的海登·克里斯滕森 (Hayden Christensen) 在 2023 年告诉《综艺》杂志，描绘他的黑暗面之旅“使他变得人性化”，但同时也透露出他是一个“可悲的人”，并且“陷入了也许他并不真正想要的生活”。
你可能会合理地推测，与被削弱的特朗普有关的保守派影响者如今是否也处于类似的境地。只是不要指望他们会承认这种中介焦虑的爆发实际上是令人畏缩的应对方式。无论选举结果如何，他们很快就会有一个新的有抱负的反英雄——这一次，你不敢嘲笑他们非常重要的职位。

title_en: In Alaska fishing community, the Dan Sullivan episode takes an ominous turn as FBI comes knocking
title_zh: 在阿拉斯加渔业社区，丹·沙利文事件随着联邦调查局的到来而出现不祥的转折
summary: In the sleepy Alaskan fishing community of Petersburg, nobody has seen Dan J
summary_zh: 在彼得堡沉睡的阿拉斯加捕鱼社区，没有人见过丹·J
body_en: In Alaska fishing community, the Dan Sullivan episode takes an ominous turn as FBI comes knocking
In the sleepy Alaskan fishing community of Petersburg, nobody has seen Dan J
By JOSHUA GOODMAN Associated Press and JIM MUSTIAN Associated Press
PETERSBURG, Alaska -- In the sleepy Alaskan fishing community of Petersburg, nobody has seen Dan J. Sullivan for weeks.

His rustic home stood dark a day after FBI agents visited friends who donated to his quixotic campaign to unseat the Republican senator with the same first and last name — Dan S. Sullivan. The only display of politics at his home was a yard sign from the League of Women Voters: “Stand Up for Democracy: Vote 2026.”

What may have begun as a ploy to harm the reelection prospects of Sen. Sullivan has taken a serious turn as the Trump administration weighs criminal charges over a campaign tactic known as “ballot stacking.”

“It just seems like such a waste of our taxpayer money,” said Sharon Hunter, a Petersburg resident who, with her husband, donated $1,000 to Dan J. Sullivan, a former elementary school teacher. FBI agents knocked on her door Saturday during a round of interviews with the campaign’s dozen contributors.
“I’m a bit incredulous about their whole angle,” Hunter said, “because they’re targeting a person who’s been a real contributor in this community.”

Recruiting candidates to draw votes away from an opponent has been a part of Alaska's quirky politics for years. This time around, the state's open primary and ranked choice voting systems add another wrinkle, making it easier for lesser-known candidates to play spoilers when no contender secures a majority.

The tactic has drawn fresh scrutiny as the incumbent Sullivan fights off a serious challenge from Democrat Mary Peltola, a former U.S. representative, in a race that could determine control of the Senate.

Peltola has denied any role in the alleged chicanery as she has sought to distance herself from a New York Times article published last week that linked a group backing the former congresswoman to a Democratic operative trying to recruit decoy candidates.
“This is Alaska. We’re not in the business of tricking each other up here,” Peltola told supporters at a rally in Anchorage last week.

Dan J. Sullivan’s entry into the race has drawn scrutiny since June, when the Alaska Division of Elections tried to remove him from the primary ballot, determining he had not filed his candidacy as a Republican in “good faith.” That finding was overturned by state courts. To avoid any confusion, state officials identify Dan S. Sullivan on the ballot as a Republican and the incumbent.

Dan J. Sullivan repeatedly said he entered the race on his own accord and had no contact with Peltola's campaign — “zero, none, zilch,” he told The Associated Press in June. He answered “no” when asked if any Democratic operatives had contacted him to run.

A federal lawsuit brought by the Trump administration to revive efforts to undermine the former teacher's candidacy — and challenge a potential Peltola win by blocking certification of the election results — was dismissed on Sunday by a federal judge. The Justice Department quickly appealed.
AP's efforts to reach Dan J. Sullivan since The Times article have been unsuccessful. Several of the donors AP interviewed said they have not spoken to him in quite some time.
The senator, meanwhile, is seeking to ride the controversy to a third term.
“My costume is the real Dan Sullivan – not the fake guy,” he quipped to trick-or-treaters Saturday night.

The controversy has thrust Petersburg, a fishing community of 3,000 known as “Little Norway” for its late 19th century settlers, into the center of a federal investigation and a crush of media attention.

It's the type of small town where everyone seems to know everyone else’s business, and more than a dozen residents said they liked and admired Dan J. Sullivan, calling him a creative teacher who ran an after-school program, Little Kids Rock, to teach guitar.
body_zh: 在阿拉斯加渔业社区，丹·沙利文事件随着联邦调查局的到来而出现不祥的转折
在彼得堡沉睡的阿拉斯加捕鱼社区，没有人见过丹·J
约书亚·古德曼 (JOSHUA GOODMAN) 美联社和吉姆·穆斯蒂安 (JIM MUSTIAN) 美联社报道
阿拉斯加圣彼得堡——在圣彼得堡沉睡的阿拉斯加渔业社区，已经好几个星期没有人见过丹·J·沙利文了。
一天前，联邦调查局探员拜访了一些朋友，这些朋友为他的堂吉诃德式竞选活动捐款，以推翻同名的共和党参议员丹·S·沙利文(Dan S. Sullivan)，一天后，他乡村的家一片漆黑。他家里唯一的政治展示是女性选民联盟的院子标志：“支持民主：2026 年投票”。
随着特朗普政府考虑对“堆积选票”的竞选策略提出刑事指控，这一原本可能是损害参议员沙利文连任前景的策略已经发生了严重转变。
圣彼得堡居民莎伦·亨特 (Sharon Hunter) 说：“这似乎浪费了我们纳税人的钱。”她和丈夫一起向前小学教师丹·J·沙利文 (Dan J. Sullivan) 捐赠了 1,000 美元。周六，联邦调查局特工在对竞选活动的十几名贡献者进行一轮采访时敲开了她的门。
“我对他们的整个角度有点怀疑，”亨特说，“因为他们的目标是一个为这个社区做出真正贡献的人。”
多年来，招募候选人来吸引对手选票一直是阿拉斯加古怪政治的一部分。这一次，该州的公开初选和排名选择投票系统又增加了一个问题，当没有竞争者获得多数席位时，不太知名的候选人更容易搅局。
随着现任议员沙利文在一场可能决定参议院控制权的竞选中击败前美国众议员、民主党人玛丽·佩尔托拉的严峻挑战，这一策略受到了新的审视。
佩尔托拉否认参与了所谓的欺骗行为，因为她试图与《纽约时报》上周发表的一篇文章保持距离，该文章将支持这位前国会女议员的团体与试图招募诱饵候选人的民主党特工联系起来。
“这是阿拉斯加。我们不会在这里互相欺骗，”佩尔托拉上周在安克雷奇的一次集会上对支持者说。
自 6 月以来，丹·J·沙利文 (Dan J. Sullivan) 的竞选就受到了密切关注，当时阿拉斯加选举部试图将他从初选中剔除，认为他没有“善意”地提交共和党候选人资格。该裁决被州法院推翻。为了避免任何混淆，州政府官员在选票上确认丹·S·沙利文 (Dan S. Sullivan) 为共和党人和现任总统。
丹·J·沙利文 (Dan J. Sullivan) 一再表示，他是自愿参加竞选的，与佩尔托拉的竞选活动没有任何联系——“零，没有，没有，”他在 6 月份告诉美联社。当被问及是否有民主党工作人员联系他竞选时，他回答“没有”。
特朗普政府提起的一项联邦诉讼，旨在重新努力破坏这位前教师的候选资格，并通过阻止选举结果的认证来挑战佩尔托拉可能获胜的努力，但周日被一名联邦法官驳回。司法部很快提出上诉。
自《泰晤士报》发表文章以来，美联社试图联系丹·J·沙利文，但没有成功。美联社采访的几位捐助者表示，他们已经很长一段时间没有与他交谈了。
与此同时，这位参议员正在寻求将这场争议延续到第三个任期。
“我的服装是真正的丹·沙利文，而不是假人，”周六晚上他对“不给糖就捣蛋”的人打趣道。
这场争议将圣彼得堡这个拥有 3000 人的渔业社区，因其 19 世纪末的定居者而被称为“小挪威”，成为联邦调查和媒体关注的中心。
在这种小镇上，每个人似乎都知道其他人的事，十几名居民表示他们喜欢并钦佩 Dan J. Sullivan，称他为一位富有创造力的老师，负责开展课后项目“Little Kids Rock”，教授吉他。

title_en: With AO3 down, fanfic readers are in survival mode
title_zh: AO3 宕机后，同人读者陷入生存模式
summary: When the internet’s biggest fanfiction repository vanishes from reach, there’s one thing you can still count on: a network of fellow fans.
summary_zh: 当互联网上最大的同人小说库消失时，你仍然可以依靠一件事：同人粉丝网络。
body_en: When the internet’s biggest fanfiction repository vanishes from reach, there’s one thing you can still count on: a network of fellow fans.
Just ask the massive community of Archive of Our Own readers, who in the past few days have gone from panic to ingenuity after their beloved fanfic haven went dark.

AO3 is home to more than 18 million works, including many sexually explicit stories (affectionately referred to as “smut”), and writing inspired by popular IP, such as “Harry Potter,” “Twilight” and “Heated Rivalry.”
But last week, the Organization for Transformative Works, the nonprofit behind AO3, announced the site would be down for two to four weeks, citing a “ security incident .”

The prospect of weeks without AO3 sent shock waves through a community devoted to the platform’s uncensored storytelling and meticulous tagging system. Some went as far as likening the outage to life in prehistoric times or descending into madness .
But their desperation also gave way to solidarity, with readers sharing tips with each other on how they can still get their fan fiction fix.

In the r/AO3 community on Reddit, moderators have set up megathreads for the purpose of helping members find and share copies of their favorite stories. Some AO3 writers are uploading new chapters of their fanfiction stories to their Tumblr blogs. Others are creating shared Google folders.

“There are always debates, different opinions and occasional fights within and between fandoms. But during the outage, I have seen people from completely different fandoms and backgrounds helping one another and working toward shared solutions,” said Ashmita, a 23-year-old AO3 reader and fanfiction writer from India who built a web tool to make it easier for users to connect Google Drive folders and navigate the hundreds or thousands of files inside.
“It has been a beautiful reminder of how much these communities care about each other,” Ashmita, who requested to be identified by first name only to preserve her online privacy, added.
Another public Google Drive link to a “ Fanfic Emergency Fund ,” created by author Berklie Novak-Stolz, has already accrued a deluge of works across a wide range of fandoms and genres.
“The horrors may persist, but so do we,” Novak-Stolz wrote in a letter to readers. “We’re all going to be okay thanks to the wonders of humanness and community and storytelling.”
As of Sunday, the Organization for Transformative Works said there are no further updates regarding the outage.

The organization encouraged users to review certain recommended safety practices as the outage persists, such as clicking links from trusted sources, being wary of scammers and creating unique passwords for every website.

In a statement to NBC News, a spokesperson for the Organization for Transformative Works said it will share further updates on the “security incident” as soon as verified information becomes available.

“AO3 and the OTW were founded by fans, for fans. That ethos remains at the heart of our mission today, and we love seeing how fans mobilize and support one another, both through and beyond AO3,” the spokesperson said. “As fan[s] ourselves, we deeply empathize with the frustration and despair of losing access to AO3—and we’re heartened by the creativity, humor, and sense of community reflected in the flood of memes.”
AO3’s absence has prompted other fanfiction websites and adjacent platforms to seize on an opportunity to attract more users.
“We’re here to support you during this difficult time,” a post from Wattpad on X read .
“while our spouse ao3 is still resting drop your fav fanfics and authors to fill the void,” the X account for Tumblr wrote.
The audio erotica platform Quinn also enticed readers by offering a discount code citing AO3’s blackout.
But some die-hard readers said there’s nothing like AO3, a space they laud for being entirely community-funded and free of advertisements.
body_zh: 当互联网上最大的同人小说库消失时，你仍然可以依靠一件事：同人粉丝网络。
只要问问《我们自己的档案馆》的广大读者群体就知道了，在过去的几天里，在他们心爱的同人天堂陷入黑暗之后，他们从恐慌变成了聪明才智。
AO3 拥有超过 1800 万部作品，其中包括许多露骨的色情故事（被亲切地称为“色情内容”），以及受流行 IP 启发的作品，例如《哈利·波特》、《暮光之城》和《激烈的竞争》。
但上周，AO3 背后的非营利组织变革工作组织 (Organization for Transformative Works) 宣布该网站将关闭两到四个星期，理由是发生了“安全事件”。
AO3 几周没有上线的前景给致力于该平台未经审查的故事讲述和细致的标签系统的社区带来了冲击。有些人甚至将这次停电比作史前时代的生活或陷入疯狂。
但他们的绝望也让位给了团结，读者们互相分享如何仍然能够修复同人小说的技巧。
在 Reddit 上的 r/AO3 社区中，版主设立了超级线程，旨在帮助成员找到并分享他们最喜欢的故事的副本。一些 AO3 作家正在将同人小说的新章节上传到他们的 Tumblr 博客。其他人正在创建共享的 Google 文件夹。
“同人圈内部和同人圈之间总是存在争论、不同意见和偶尔的争斗。但在停运期间，我看到来自完全不同的同人圈和背景的人们互相帮助并致力于共享解决方案，”来自印度的 23 岁 AO3 读者和同人小说作家阿什米塔 (Ashmita) 说，他开发了一个网络工具，使用户可以更轻松地连接 Google Drive 文件夹并浏览其中的数百或数千个文件。
“这很好地提醒了我们这些社区是多么关心彼此，”阿什米塔补充道。为了保护自己的在线隐私，她要求只透露名字。
另一个由作家 Berklie Novak-Stolz 创建的“同人小说紧急基金”的公开 Google 云端硬盘链接已经积累了大量跨同人圈和流派的作品。
诺瓦克-斯托尔茨在给读者的信中写道：“恐怖可能会持续存在，但我们也会持续存在。” “感谢人性、社区和讲故事的奇迹，我们都会好起来的。”
截至周日，变革工作组织表示，没有有关停电的进一步更新。
该组织鼓励用户在中断持续存在时查看某些推荐的安全做法，例如点击来自可信来源的链接、警惕诈骗者以及为每个网站创建唯一的密码。
变革工作组织的发言人在给 NBC 新闻的一份声明中表示，一旦获得经过验证的信息，该组织将立即分享有关“安全事件”的进一步更新。
“AO3 和 OTW 是由粉丝创立，为粉丝服务的。这种精神仍然是我们今天使命的核心，我们很高兴看到粉丝们如何通过 AO3 内外动员起来并相互支持，”该发言人说道。 “作为我们自己的粉丝，我们对失去 AO3 的访问权限深表同情，并且我们对大量表情包中所体现的创造力、幽默感和社区意识感到鼓舞。”
AO3的缺席促使其他同人网站和邻近平台抓住机会吸引更多用户。
Wattpad 在 X 上发布的一篇帖子写道：“在这个困难时期，我们会为您提供支持。”
“当我们的配偶 ao3 还在休息时，请放下你最喜欢的同人小说和作者来填补空白，”Tumblr 的 X 账户写道。
音频色情平台 Quinn 还以 AO3 停电为由提供折扣代码来吸引读者。
但一些顽固读者表示，没有什么比 AO3 更好的了，他们称赞这个空间完全由社区资助且没有广告。

title_en: Trump administration's social media posts ahead of elections criticized for being inflammatory
title_zh: 特朗普政府在选举前的社交媒体帖子被批评具有煽动性
summary: The Trump administration’s online accounts have circulated images of a pumpkin carved with a sombrero design and a fake Halloween-themed background around a Black man apparently accused of food assistance fraud
summary_zh: 特朗普政府的在线账户流传了雕刻有宽边帽设计的南瓜和假万圣节主题背景的图片。
body_en: Trump administration's social media posts ahead of elections criticized for being inflammatory

The Trump administration’s online accounts have circulated images of a pumpkin carved with a sombrero design and a fake Halloween-themed background around a Black man apparently accused of food assistance fraud

The Trump administration’s online accounts are circulating images of a pumpkin carved with a sombrero design and a fake Halloween-themed background around a Black man apparently accused of food assistance fraud, in social media posts slammed by critics as inflammatory rhetoric.

Only days before the midterm elections, the posts coincide with the government’s sweeping campaign to show its aggressive immigration enforcement , and highlight efforts to crack down on fraud to save taxpayers money when rising healthcare costs and other economic stressors have made affordability a top voter concern.

Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins posted Saturday on the social platform X a photo of the Black man standing in front of stacks of what appear to be U.S. currency with the headline, SNAP FRAUDSTER, an apparent reference to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, formerly known as food stamps.
He is holding aloft what appears to be a bill set aflame.
“Some costumes come with a price tag. This one comes with a prison sentence,” it says to the backdrop of fake Spirit Halloween costume packaging.
Another photo posted by the White House on X on Thursday showed a pumpkin with the shape of a sombrero carved across it and the words “Spooky szn is here.”

The post by Rollins, who was nominated by Trump to serve as the U.S. Secretary of Agriculture in November 2024, appears to be taken from an Instagram post from September 2025 by an account under the name Shawty Dred.

Earlier this month, Mercedes Reshard New, identified by the Justice Department as a social media personality also known as “Shawty Dred,” was arrested on federal charges for fraudulently obtaining more than $4 million in Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits in Georgia.
It’s not the first time the White House has been accused of posting inflammatory images on official government social media accounts.

Just over a year ago during the government shutdown, the White House revived a deepfake video posted by Trump of House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries in a fake mustache and sombrero to accuse the Democrats of acting on behalf of illegal immigrants instead of U.S. citizens. Jeffries described the meme as bigoted. They played it on repeat in the White House briefing room, though Vice President JD Vance promised that the “sombrero memes will stop” when Democrats agreed to end the shutdown.
The NAACP did not respond to an email seeking comment, nor did the White House or Rollins.
Learjet with 9 aboard crashes in Palm Beach County, Florida: FAA
Sen. Chris Murphy hospitalized after suffering a stroke, chief of staff says
2 college students found dead after going missing while hiking, police say

The Trump administration in recent weeks has ratcheted up its anti-immigrant rhetoric and accusations of fraud, including against U.S. Rep. Ilhan Omar whose Washington, D.C., home was searched by federal agents earlier this month. Federal authorities are investigating potential fraud in her family’s immigration paperwork. Omar, who was born in Somalia, is a naturalized U.S. citizen.

It also has taken a series of punitive steps linked to allegations of fraud in mostly Democratic-led states , including California and Minnesota whose governors accused the federal government of targeting their states for political reasons.

Federal prosecutors said in a news release Oct. 21 that the influencer, New, controlled more than 350 fraudulent SNAP accounts under stolen identities between January 2020 and July 2026. He allegedly applied for his company, Shawty Dred LLC, to become an authorized SNAP retailer and used EBT debit cards to extract about $4 million from the accounts.

New’s Instagram account, which has more than two million followers, has flaunted his extravagant lifestyle, federal prosecutors said. Posts depict him flying on private jets, posing with Rolls-Royce vehicles in front of his “super mansion,” and handling massive stacks of cash.
body_zh: 特朗普政府在选举前的社交媒体帖子被批评具有煽动性
特朗普政府的在线账户流传了一个雕刻有宽边帽设计的南瓜和一个假万圣节主题背景的图像，围绕着一名显然被指控食品援助欺诈的黑人
特朗普政府的网络账户在社交媒体帖子中传播了雕刻有宽边帽设计的南瓜和假万圣节主题背景围绕一名显然被指控食品援助欺诈的黑人的图片，这些图片被批评者抨击为煽动性言论。
就在中期选举前几天，这些帖子恰逢政府开展大规模宣传活动，以展示其积极的移民执法，并强调在医疗费用上涨和其他经济压力因素使负担能力成为选民最关心的问题之际，打击欺诈行为以节省纳税人的钱。
农业部长布鲁克·罗林斯周六在社交平台 X 上发布了一张黑人男子站在一堆看似美元的货币前的照片，标题为“SNAP FRAUDSTER”，显然是指补充营养援助计划（以前称为食品券）。
他高举着一张似乎已着火的钞票。
“有些服装带有价格标签。这款服装则需被判入狱，”它在假冒的精神万圣节服装包装的背景下说道。
周四，白宫在 X 上发布的另一张照片显示，一个南瓜上刻着宽边帽的形状，上面写着“Spooky szn is here”。
罗林斯于 2024 年 11 月被特朗普提名担任美国农业部长，他的帖子似乎取自 Shawty Dred 帐户于 2025 年 9 月发布的 Instagram 帖子。
本月早些时候，梅塞德斯·雷沙德·纽（Mercedes Reshard New）被司法部认定为社交媒体名人，也被称为“Shawty Dred”，因联邦指控在佐治亚州以欺诈手段获取超过 400 万美元的补充营养援助计划福利而被捕。
这并不是白宫第一次被指控在政府官方社交媒体账户上发布煽动性图片。
就在一年多前，政府关门期间，白宫重新播放了特朗普发布的一段深度假视频，视频中众议院民主党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯戴着假胡子和宽边帽，指责民主党代表非法移民而不是美国公民行事。杰弗里斯形容这个模因是偏执的。他们在白宫简报室重复播放了这段视频，尽管副总统 JD 万斯承诺，当民主党同意结束政府关门时，“宽边帽模因将会停止”。
全国有色人种协进会没有回复寻求置评的电子邮件，白宫或罗林斯也没有回复。
载有 9 人的里尔喷气式飞机在佛罗里达州棕榈滩县坠毁：美国联邦航空局 (FAA)
参谋长称参议员克里斯·墨菲中风后入院治疗
警方称，两名大学生在徒步旅行中失踪后被发现死亡
最近几周，特朗普政府加大了反移民言论和欺诈指控，其中包括针对美国众议员伊尔汗·奥马尔(Ilhan Omar)的欺诈指控，本月早些时候，联邦特工搜查了他在华盛顿特区的家。联邦当局正在调查她家人的移民文件中潜在的欺诈行为。奥马尔出生于索马里，已入籍美国公民。
它还针对大多数民主党领导的州的欺诈指控采取了一系列惩罚措施，其中包括加利福尼亚州和明尼苏达州，这两个州的州长指责联邦政府出于政治原因针对其州。
联邦检察官在 10 月 21 日的新闻稿中表示，网红 New 在 2020 年 1 月至 2026 年 7 月期间以被盗身份控制了 350 多个欺诈性 SNAP 账户。据称，他向自己的公司 Shawty Dred LLC 申请成为 SNAP 授权零售商，并使用 EBT 借记卡从账户中提取了约 400 万美元。
联邦检察官称，纽的 Instagram 账户拥有超过 200 万粉丝，该账户一直在炫耀他奢华的生活方式。帖子描述了他乘坐私人飞机、在他的“超级豪宅”前与劳斯莱斯汽车合影、处理大量现金。

title_en: Trump to Axios: "No rush" to decide on bombing Iran again
title_zh: 特朗普对 Axios 表示：“不急于”再次决定轰炸伊朗
summary: President Trump told Axios in a phone interview Monday he's "in no rush" to decide whether to resume fighting in Iran . Why it matters: The midterm elections have been seen as an inflection point for Trump on whether to unleash a massive bombing campaign to tr
summary_zh: 特朗普总统周一在电话采访中告诉 Axios，他“不急于”决定是否恢复伊朗战斗。为什么重要：中期选举
body_en: President Trump told Axios in a phone interview Monday he's "in no rush" to decide whether to resume fighting in Iran .
Why it matters: The midterm elections have been seen as an inflection point for Trump on whether to unleash a massive bombing campaign to try to bring the war to an end.
But it appears the president, at least for now, will continue on dual tracks — letting negotiations play out while preparing to go back to war if he concludes a deal isn't reachable.

What he is saying: "One way or the other, we will do something, but there is no rush. We crippled them financially. They have no money, no gasoline and their people are getting very tired of it," Trump said in the interview.

Driving the news: Qatari mediators have written a draft agreement outlining a three-day sequence of confidence-building measures aimed at resuming direct U.S.-Iran negotiations, according to regional sources.

A diplomat with knowledge of the situation said the Qatari mediators are waiting for feedback from the U.S. and Iran. Qatari mediator Ali al-Thawadi traveled to Tehran on Monday to continue talks on the draft agreement and the diplomat said progress is building.
Trump is giving diplomacy a chance but is clear-eyed about the chances of reaching a deal.

"We are talking to them. It's going fine. The problem with them is ... they try and tap tap tap [us along]. There's less urgency [on the Iranian side] than you think there would be, but they want to make a deal more than they ever wanted," Trump said.
Between the lines: Trump is weighing three courses of action, backed by three different camps
1. Make a deal: Vice President JD Vance and White House envoy Steve Witkoff are urging him to move toward a deal because a renewed war might not change the situation for the better.
Most Gulf countries support this position and have communicated that to Trump, sources say.

2. Go back to battle: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu wants to resume combat, as does Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth. They argue that Iran can't be trusted to make a deal let alone abide by one, and that Trump should finish the job militarily.

3. Maximum economic pain: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, CIA Director John Ratcliffe and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are advising Trump to maintain the "no war, no deal" status quo and allow the economic pressure campaign to continue, sources said.

Ratcliffe told Trump that prolonged economic pain will induce Iran to make more concessions — or create enough instability inside the country that citizens revolt, a source with direct knowledge said. The CIA declined to comment.
The other side: Iran's civilian leadership sounded hopeful on Monday about the prospects of reaching a deal.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei "granted the government certain authorities" to try to reach an agreement through diplomacy.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Monday that the diplomatic exchanges "have become very intensive."

"Qatar and Pakistan are playing very active roles as mediators. We have presented our conditions and our proposal, and everything depends on Washington's political rationality. If they choose genuine diplomacy, we are ready to engage. But if they intend to engage in deception and military operations, they will face a response more painful and severe than in the past," he said.
Araghchi said that if the U.S. accepts Tehran's conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, then "negotiations will resume."
"Otherwise, the current situation will continue, and Iran will not bow down," he said.
body_zh: 特朗普总统周一在电话采访中告诉 Axios，他“不急于”决定是否恢复伊朗战斗。
为什么重要：中期选举被视为特朗普是否发动大规模轰炸行动以试图结束战争的转折点。
但至少目前看来，总统将继续走双轨路线——一边让谈判继续进行，一边准备在认为无法达成协议的情况下重返战争。
他在说什么：“不管怎样，我们会做点什么，但不要着急。我们在经济上削弱了他们。他们没有钱，没有汽油，他们的人民对此感到非常厌倦，”特朗普在采访中说。
推动这一消息的是：据地区消息人士称，卡塔尔调解人已起草了一份协议草案，概述了旨在恢复美国与伊朗直接谈判的为期三天的一系列建立信任措施。
一位了解情况的外交官表示，卡塔尔调解人正在等待美国和伊朗的反馈。卡塔尔调解员阿里·塔瓦迪周一前往德黑兰继续就协议草案进行谈判，这位外交官表示进展正在取得进展。
特朗普正在给予外交机会，但他对达成协议的可能性有着清醒的认识。
“我们正在与他们交谈。一切进展顺利。他们的问题是……他们试图[我们一起]。[伊朗方面]的紧迫性没有你想象的那么紧迫，但他们比他们想要的更想要达成协议，”特朗普说。
字里行间：特朗普正在考虑三个不同阵营支持的三项行动方案
1.达成协议：副总统万斯和白宫特使史蒂夫·威特科夫敦促他达成协议，因为新的战争可能不会让局势变得更好。
消息人士称，大多数海湾国家支持这一立场，并已向特朗普传达了这一立场。
2.重返战场：以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡和国防部长皮特·赫格斯都希望恢复战斗。他们认为，不能相信伊朗会达成协议，更不用说遵守协议了，特朗普应该以军事手段完成这项任务。
3.最大的经济痛苦：消息人士称，财政部长斯科特·贝森特、中央情报局局长约翰·拉特克利夫和国务卿马可·卢比奥建议特朗普维持“不战争，不达成协议”的现状，并允许经济压力运动继续下去。
一位知情人士称，拉特克利夫告诉特朗普，长期的经济痛苦将促使伊朗做出更多让步，或者在国内造成足够的不稳定，导致公民反抗。中央情报局拒绝发表评论。
另一方面：伊朗文职领导层周一似乎对达成协议的前景充满希望。
伊朗总统马苏德·佩泽什基安表示，最高领袖哈梅内伊“授予政府某些权力”，以试图通过外交达成协议。
伊朗外交部长阿巴斯·阿拉格奇周一表示，外交交流“变得非常密集”。
“卡塔尔和巴基斯坦作为调解人发挥着非常积极的作用。我们提出了我们的条件和建议，一切都取决于华盛顿的政治理性。如果他们选择真正的外交，我们准备参与。但如果他们打算进行欺骗和军事行动，他们将面临比过去更加痛苦和严厉的反应，”他说。
阿拉格奇表示，如果美国接受德黑兰重新开放霍尔木兹海峡的条件，那么“谈判将会恢复”。
“否则，目前的局势将持续下去，伊朗也不会屈服，”他说。

title_en: Scoop: Senate GOP makes massive bet on streaming
title_zh: 独家新闻：参议院共和党在流媒体上下了重注
summary: The top Senate GOP super PAC has nearly tripled its spending on streaming and social media platforms this election cycle to more than $200 million, Axios has learned. Why it matters : In a record cycle for ad spending, more political money is shifting to strea
summary_zh: Axe 表示，参议院共和党最高政治行动委员会在本次选举周期中在流媒体和社交媒体平台上的支出几乎增加了两倍，达到 2 亿美元以上
body_en: The top Senate GOP super PAC has nearly tripled its spending on streaming and social media platforms this election cycle to more than $200 million, Axios has learned.

Why it matters : In a record cycle for ad spending, more political money is shifting to streaming, where super PACs have greater freedom to target voters, bargain and experiment — but platforms have more power to set the rules.
In some states, streaming and social media have swallowed half of the Senate Leadership Fund (SLF) budget, according to a source familiar with the group's spending.
SLF's $200M+ total for the 2026 cycle (up from $71M in 2024) includes tens of millions of dollars funneled through the SLF-linked Texas PAC and its affiliated nonprofit One Nation.
The other side: The top Senate Democratic super PAC declined to provide a dollar figure for their spending on streaming.
"Senate Majority PAC invested more this cycle in digital communications than any previous cycle, running digital campaigns in 12 states," SMP communications director Lauren French told Axios.
Zoom in : Streaming and social platforms offer campaigns the power to target more specific audiences compared to traditional broadcast, and make it easier to measure the impact.
"Its way more surgical than a linear broadcast buy," Zack Roday, managing director at Think Big, told Axios.
But platforms can also set their own rules around which types of ads they want to accept. Some, like Netflix and TikTok, don't allow any candidate or issue ads .
Republicans have complained about restrictions on ads that include transgender issues on Disney-owned platforms.
Between the lines: Super PACs often pay multiple times what a campaign pays for ads on broadcast TV and radio because of laws ensuring candidates get the lowest rates.
Online, super PACs can negotiate directly — and use their fat budgets and sprawling election maps as leverage.
SLF works with platforms like SiriusXM, Paramount, Hulu, YouTube and others to lock in discounts based on their overall spending plans, according to the source.
Groups can also experiment with different lengths and formats for ads online, breaking the 30-second broadcast mold.
What to watch: Streaming ads can also be trickier for outside tracking. While Meta and Google provide public data on political ad buys, not every platform provides that kind of visibility
Streaming buys aren't covered by the same FCC filing requirements as political ad reservations on broadcast TV and radio.
Broadcast filings can offer a preview of a group's targets months in advance, but streaming reservations are much harder to see.
Although AI is changing the game, and there is a growing industry of companies offering better tracking tools.
Super PACs still have to report independent expenditures to the FEC through 24- and 48- hour reports.
Zoom out: Strong grassroots fundraising has helped Democratic candidates crush Republicans in dollars brought in directly to candidates.
body_zh: Axios 获悉，参议院共和党最高政治行动委员会在本次选举周期中在流媒体和社交媒体平台上的支出几乎增加了两倍，达到 2 亿多美元。
重要性：在广告支出创纪录的周期中，更多的政治资金正在转向流媒体，其中超级政治行动委员会有更大的自由来瞄准选民、讨价还价和实验——但平台有更多的权力来制定规则。
据熟悉参议院领导基金 (SLF) 支出的消息人士透露，在一些州，流媒体和社交媒体已经吞噬了参议院领导基金 (SLF) 预算的一半。
SLF 2026 年周期的总资金超过 2 亿美元（高于 2024 年的 7100 万美元），其中包括通过与 SLF 相关的德克萨斯州 PAC 及其附属非营利组织 One Nation 输送的数千万美元。
另一面：参议院民主党超级政治行动委员会拒绝提供其流媒体支出的美元数字。
SMP 传播总监 Lauren French 告诉 Axios：“参议院多数党 PAC 本周期在数字通信方面的投入比以往任何周期都多，在 12 个州开展了数字活动。”
放大：与传统广播相比，流媒体和社交平台为活动提供了针对更具体受众的能力，并且更容易衡量影响。
Think Big 董事总经理扎克·罗迪 (Zack Roday) 告诉 Axios：“这比线性广播购买更具手术性。”
但平台也可以围绕他们想要接受的广告类型制定自己的规则。有些，例如 Netflix 和 TikTok，不允许任何候选广告或发布广告。
共和党人抱怨迪士尼旗下平台上对包含变性问题的广告的限制。
言外之意是：由于法律确保候选人获得最低费率，超级政治行动委员会通常支付竞选活动在广播电视和广播上的广告费用的数倍。
超级政治行动委员会可以在网上直接进行谈判，并利用其丰厚的预算和庞大的选举地图作为杠杆。
消息人士称，SLF 与 SiriusXM、派拉蒙、Hulu、YouTube 等平台合作，根据他们的总体支出计划锁定折扣。
团体还可以尝试不同长度和格式的在线广告，打破 30 秒的广播模式。
看点：流媒体广告对于外部跟踪来说也比较棘手。虽然 Meta 和 Google 提供有关政治广告购买的公共数据，但并非每个平台都提供这种可见性
流媒体购买不受与广播电视和广播上的政治广告预订相同的 FCC 备案要求的约束。
广播备案可以提前几个月提供团体目标的预览，但流媒体预订则更难看到。
尽管人工智能正在改变游戏规则，并且越来越多的公司提供更好的跟踪工具。
超级政治行动委员会仍然必须通过 24 小时和 48 小时报告向 FEC 报告独立支出。
缩小范围：强大的草根筹款帮助民主党候选人在直接向候选人提供的资金方面击败了共和党人。

Snap settles lawsuit accusing platform of fueling teen depression and eating disorders

Snap has reached a settlement in a lawsuit brought by two teenagers who accused the company of designing its platform to be addictive and contributing to their depression, anxiety, and eating disorders, as first reported by Reuters . The plaintiffs had previously reached settlements with Meta, TikTok, and YouTube.

The trial was set to be Snap’s first in a broader wave of litigation over social media’s impact on young users. The company had already settled its other cases scheduled for trial. Snap CEO Evan Spiegel was expected to take the stand.

The plaintiffs said they started using YouTube as young as age 3 and other social media platforms at around age 9. They said they developed compulsive usage habits, which they attributed to features such as autoplay and infinite scrolling.

“The Parties are pleased to have been able to resolve this matter in an amicable manner,” a Snap spokesperson said in a statement to TechCrunch. “We’ve built safeguards, launched safety tutorials, and partnered with experts and because safety is never finished, we remain committed to continually strengthening the safety, privacy, and well-being of our community.”

OpenAI pitches data center power plants as a way to protect nearby areas
As public opinion has soured on data centers, it’s selling ‘AI campuses’ as protectors, instead of noisy polluters.
Emma Roth is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

In an announcement on Monday , OpenAI says it will pilot its “Grid Protectors Program” at an upcoming data center in Effingham County, Georgia, where the company promises to free up to 1,000 megawatts of power during extreme weather or emergencies, enough to power air conditioners in around 700,000 homes.

The announcement comes as opposition to data centers spreads across the US, in response to massive projects that have begun development and construction, frequently with little or no input from local residents. In Utah, residents protested after Box Elder County commissioners signed off on a data center expected to consume more than double the state’s peak electricity demand in 2025, and spread hot air in the desert valley surrounding the data center.

Now OpenAI’s approach is to pitch the construction of power plants that feed the electricity required by the new AI data centers it’s building as “a resource that utilities can call on when communities need it most.”

Several states like Tennessee, Florida, Oklahoma, Oregon, and others have enacted laws that say they will prevent AI companies from passing energy costs on to residents, in addition to moratoriums and other restrictions. This is besides the environmental impacts, as a recent study by the Houston Advanced Research Center (HARC) said that powering proposed Texas data center projects could undo decades of air quality gains over just five years.
Sam Altman says it’s better for RAM to be in a data center than on your desk

OpenAI, which has switched to calling its AI data centers “compute campuses” in an effort to separate from their poor public reputation , claims it helps reduce costs for customers by operating year-round

“Electricity demand also rises and falls with the seasons, with different regions facing their biggest peaks at different times,” OpenAI’s announcement says. “Our compute campuses need power year-round. With the right agreements, that steady demand can help spread the grid’s fixed costs across more electricity sales, while flexibility lets us reduce demand when the system is busiest.”

OpenAI says it’s going to continue working with policymakers and utility services to make “arrangements for our future campus to reduce electricity demand when the grid is under strain.” Along with its data center in Georgia, OpenAI is also partnering with Oracle and SoftBank to build its “Stargate” data centers across the US, including in Shackelford County, Texas; Doña Ana County, New Mexico; and Milam County, Texas.

随着公众舆论对数据中心的态度恶化，它正在出售“人工智能园区”作为保护者，而不是喧闹的污染者。
艾玛·罗斯 (Emma Roth) 是一位新闻撰稿人，报道流媒体战争、消费技术、加密货币、社交媒体等。此前，她是 MUO 的作家和编辑。
OpenAI 在周一的一份声明中表示，将在佐治亚州埃芬汉县即将建成的数据中心试行其“电网保护者计划”，该公司承诺在极端天气或紧急情况下释放高达 1,000 兆瓦的电力，足以为大约 700,000 户家庭的空调供电。
这一消息发布之际，美国各地对数据中心的反对情绪正在蔓延，以应对已经开始开发和建设的大型项目，而当地居民的意见往往很少或根本没有。在犹他州，博克斯埃尔德县专员签署了一个数据中心的批准，该数据中心预计将在 2025 年消耗该州峰值电力需求的两倍以上，并在数据中心周围的沙漠山谷中传播热空气，引发居民抗议。
现在，OpenAI 的方法是宣传发电厂的建设，为其正在建设的新人工智能数据中心提供所需的电力，并将其视为“公用事业公司在社区最需要时可以调用的资源”。
田纳西州、佛罗里达州、俄克拉荷马州、俄勒冈州等几个州已经颁布了法律，除了暂停和其他限制外，还将阻止人工智能公司将能源成本转嫁给居民。这还不包括对环境的影响，休斯敦高级研究中心 (HARC) 最近的一项研究表明，为拟议的德克萨斯州数据中心项目供电可能会在短短五年内抵消数十年的空气质量改善。
Sam Altman 表示，RAM 放在数据中心比放在办公桌上更好
OpenAI 已改称其人工智能数据中心为“计算园区”，以摆脱其糟糕的公众声誉，并声称通过全年运营有助于降低客户成本
OpenAI 的公告称：“电力需求也会随着季节的变化而上升和下降，不同地区在不同的时间面临最大的峰值。” “我们的计算园区全年都需要电力。通过正确的协议，稳定的需求可以帮助将电网的固定成本分摊到更多的电力销售上，而灵活性可以让我们在系统最繁忙时减少需求。”
OpenAI 表示，将继续与政策制定者和公用事业服务机构合作，“为我们未来的园区做出安排，以在电网紧张时减少电力需求”。除了位于佐治亚州的数据中心外，OpenAI 还与甲骨文和软银合作，在美国各地建设“Stargate”数据中心，包括德克萨斯州沙克尔福德县；新墨西哥州多纳安娜县；和德克萨斯州米拉姆县。
